The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has declared the RBI Officer Grade B Phase I Result 2026 for the recruitment of Officer Grade 'B' (DR) posts under General, DEPR, and DSIM cadres (Advt. No. RBISB/DA/01/2026-27). Candidates who appeared in the Phase I online examination held on 13-14 June 2026 can now check their qualifying status, and RBI has additionally released the Phase I Score Card on 13 July 2026, showing section-wise and overall marks. This page covers the direct download link, step-by-step process, cut-off details, and the confirmed Phase II exam schedule.

RBI Officer Grade B Phase I Result 2026: What Was Released, and When

Two separate items have been made available by RBI, and candidates should not confuse them:

  • Qualifying Result List - the list of candidates shortlisted for Phase II, published on the official RBI portal shortly after the Phase I exam.
  • Phase I Score Card (with marks) - released separately on 13 July 2026, showing section-wise and overall marks for all candidates who appeared, regardless of whether they qualified for Phase II.

Source reports on the exact publication date of the initial qualifying list vary slightly; candidates are advised to rely on the official RBI portal timestamp rather than third-party aggregator dates for the precise release time.

How to Check and Download RBI Officer Grade B Phase I Result & Score Card 2026

  1. Visit the official RBI recruitment portal, opportunities.rbi.org.in, or the direct result page linked below.
  2. Look for the link titled "RBI Officer Grade B Phase I Result / Score Card 2026."
  3. Enter your Registration Number or Roll Number.
  4. Enter your Password or Date of Birth as the login credential.
  5. Complete the captcha verification.
  6. Click Submit/Login.
  7. Your Phase I result status and score card will appear on screen.
  8. Download and save a copy (PDF/screenshot) for future reference - it is required at later stages.

Direct Link to Download RBI Officer Grade B Score Card 2026: Click Here

What Details Appear on the RBI Grade B Score Card 2026

  • Candidate's Name
  • Roll Number and Registration Number
  • Category
  • Examination Name
  • Section-wise Marks (General Awareness, English Language, Quantitative Aptitude, Reasoning Ability)
  • Overall Marks Obtained and Maximum Marks
  • Qualifying Status for Phase II

Documents Required for Phase II Shortlisted Candidates

  • RBI Grade B Phase II Admit Card
  • RBI Grade B Phase I Score Card
  • Valid Photo ID Proof (Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Passport, Voter ID, Driving Licence, etc.)
  • Educational Qualification Certificates and Mark Sheets
  • Category Certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS), if applicable
  • PwBD Certificate, if applicable
  • Recent Passport-size Photographs
  • Proof of Date of Birth, if required

Important Instructions

  • Phase I is qualifying only; marks are not counted toward the final merit list.
  • RBI does not provide any provision for re-evaluation or rechecking of Phase I marks - published scores are treated as final.
  • Keep a downloaded copy of the score card safe, as it may be required as a document at the Phase II or interview stage.
  • Always verify dates and links through the official RBI portal, since third-party job portals may occasionally display outdated or unconfirmed information.

How Many Candidates Appeared

Reported candidate numbers vary slightly between sources for this session:

  • According to a Telangana Today report, a total of 1,53,752 candidates registered for the June 2026 TG TET, comprising 50,113 candidates for Paper I and 1,03,639 candidates for Paper II.
  • According to a separate report by Manabadi, 1,15,028 candidates appeared for the examination.

How to Check TG TET Result 2026

  1. Visit the official website: tgtet.aptonline.in
  2. Click on the TG TET Result 2026 link on the homepage.
  3. Enter your Hall Ticket Number.
  4. Enter your Date of Birth and select the Applied Exam Paper (Paper I / Paper II).
  5. Click Proceed.
  6. Your TG TET scorecard will be displayed on the screen.
  7. Download and print the scorecard for future reference.

Details Mentioned on the TG TET Scorecard

Based on prior TG TET scorecards, candidates can expect the following details once the result is out:

  • Candidate's Name
  • Hall Ticket Number
  • Registration Number
  • Father's Name
  • Category
  • Paper Appeared (Paper I / Paper II)
  • Marks Obtained
  • Percentage
  • Qualifying Status
  • Examination Session

If any of these details on the actual scorecard appear incorrect, candidates should contact the Department of School Education, Telangana, immediately.

Selection Process / What TG TET Qualification Means

TG TET is a minimum eligibility test, not a recruitment exam by itself. Qualifying TG TET makes a candidate eligible to apply for future teacher recruitment processes (such as TRT/DSC) conducted by the Telangana Government. Based on prior reporting, the TET score is understood to carry weightage in such recruitment exams, though the exact weightage percentage for the current cycle should be verified against the latest official recruitment notification rather than assumed from past cycles.

Qualifying TG TET does not guarantee a teaching job.

Required Documents

Candidates are advised to keep the following ready for checking and later use of the result:

  • Hall Ticket / Admit Card
  • Downloaded and printed scorecard
  • Valid photo ID proof

Not Available Officially: a specific document checklist for post-result certificate issuance has not been detailed in the available sources.

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Check the result only on the official website, tgtet.aptonline.in.
  • Avoid unofficial websites or social media links claiming to offer early or alternate result access.
  • Verify all personal details on the scorecard immediately after downloading it.
  • Keep both digital and printed copies of the scorecard safely.
  • If the official website is slow due to heavy traffic right after release, wait a few minutes rather than repeatedly refreshing.

What to Do After the TG TET Result 2026

  • Download and save the scorecard as soon as it is available.
  • Keep multiple printed copies for future use.
  • Monitor official Telangana teacher recruitment notifications.
  • Prepare educational and identity documents in advance for future verification.
  • Candidates who do not qualify this session may use their scorecard to review performance and prepare for the next TET cycle.

Important Links

Indian Army Agniveer CEE Result 2026 - How to Download

Follow these steps to download your Agniveer CEE Result 2026:

  1. Visit the official Join Indian Army website: joinindianarmy.nic.in
  2. Click on the "Agniveer Login" / "Candidate Login" section, or use the direct result link given in the Important Links table below.

  5. Open your candidate dashboard/profile.
  6. Click on the "Download Result 2026" or "CEE Result" option.
  7. Your result pass/fail status or CEE score, depending on how the Army has structured the release will appear on screen.
  8. Download and save the result as a PDF, and take a printout for your records.

Indian Army Agniveer CEE Recruitment 2026 - Vacancy Details and Eligibility

Post-wise eligibility criteria as listed by the sources reviewed are summarized below. Physical standards showed differences between the two sources see the note under the table.

Post Name Educational Qualification
Agniveer General Duty (GD) Class 10th pass with minimum 45% marks aggregate and minimum 33% in each subject
Agniveer Technical 10+2 in Science stream (Physics, Chemistry, Maths, English) with minimum 50% aggregate and 40% in each subject, OR 10+2 in any stream with a 1-year ITI course
Agniveer Clerk/Store Keeper Technical 10+2 in any stream with minimum 60% aggregate and minimum 50% in each subject; minimum 50% in English and Maths/Accounts/Book Keeping is mandatory
Agniveer Tradesman (10th Pass) Class 10th pass in any recognized board with minimum 33% in each subject
Agniveer Tradesman (8th Pass) Class 8th pass in any recognized board with minimum 33% in each subject
Agniveer GD (Women Military Police) Class 10th pass with minimum 45% aggregate and minimum 33% in each subject; candidates with a valid LMV driving license get preference for driver requirements
Sepoy Pharma 10+2 pass and D.Pharma with minimum 55% aggregate (registered with State/Pharmacy Council of India), OR B.Pharma with minimum 50% marks and registration
Soldier Technical Nursing Assistant 10+2 in Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Botany-Zoology, English) with minimum 50% aggregate and minimum 40% in each subject
JCO Religious Teacher (RT) Post-specific religious qualification (e.g., Sahastri/Acharya in Sanskrit for Pandit, Gyani in Punjabi for Granthi) plus, for most categories, a Bachelor's degree from a recognized university

Indian Army Agniveer CEE Selection Process 2026

Based on both sources, the Agniveer selection process broadly follows these stages:

  1. Common Entrance Examination (CEE) Computer-Based Test
  2. Physical Efficiency Test (PET) and Physical Measurement Test (PMT/PST)
  3. Typing/Trade Test (applicable for specific posts such as Clerk/Store Keeper Technical)
  4. Document Verification (DV)
  5. Medical Examination

Important Instructions

  • Carrying the admit card to the exam/PET-PMT venue is compulsory.
  • Keep your Enrollment Number, Registration Number, and Date of Birth handy, as these are required to check the result online.
  • If you notice any error in your declared result, contact the Indian Army recruitment authority immediately through official channels.
  • Rally and PET/PMT schedules will be notified separately keep checking the official website regularly, as this information was Not Yet Announced at the time of this article's publication.
  • Do not rely solely on third-party aggregator websites for eligibility or physical standard figures always cross-check with your zone's official notification PDF.

After conducting interviews between 6 November 2025 and 14 November 2025, MPPSC first published the selection list on 15 January 2026. Following an internal review, the Commission withdrew this list after finding a partial error and released a corrected, revised selection list along with the marks list on 8 July 2026.

Organization Name

Madhya Pradesh Public Service Commission (MPPSC) is the recruiting body for this examination. MPPSC conducted this recruitment on behalf of the Higher Education Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh.

Examination Name

The examination is officially named the Assistant Professor (Zoology) Examination 2022, referred to in the official notice as "Sahayak Pradhyapak (Pranishastra) Pariksha-2022".

Post Name

The result relates to the post of Assistant Professor, Zoology, a teaching post under the Higher Education Department of Madhya Pradesh.

Advertisement Number

This recruitment was advertised through Advertisement Number 51/2022 dated 30 December 2022, with subsequent corrigenda, including corrigendum number 11/51/2022 dated 10 September 2024.

Selection Stage Covered

This result covers the final selection stage, meaning it includes marks and outcomes from both the written examination and the interview, along with applicable guest faculty experience marks, for the 111 posts under the main (87%) part.

Merit List Availability

Yes, the merit list is available. It is published in two parts:

  • Main List: 102 candidates selected against the 111 main-part posts.
  • Supplementary (Waiting) List: 32 candidates placed on the waiting list.

How to Check the MPPSC Assistant Professor Result 2026

Follow these steps to check the result:

  1. Visit the official MPPSC website at mppsc.mp.gov.in.

  • Candidates in the supplementary (waiting) list should stay alert for any updates in case vacancies arise.
  • Candidates whose cases are under litigation should track their individual court proceedings, as their results have been kept on hold pending the final court decision.

Selection Process

The selection process for the Assistant Professor (Zoology) post consists of:

  1. Written Examination - out of 800 marks
  2. Interview - out of 100 marks
  3. Guest Faculty Experience Marks - out of 20 marks (applicable to eligible guest faculty candidates as per the advertisement, verified by a departmental committee of the Higher Education Department)

The final merit is prepared using the total of these three components, out of a maximum of 920 marks.

What Is the IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026?

This section explains the purpose of the reserve list and why IBPS issues it after the main selection round.

A reserve list is a backup panel that IBPS prepares after declaring the final result of the CRP RRBs-XIV exam. Once the primary list of selected candidates is allotted to participating banks, some vacancies remain unfilled because certain selected candidates do not join within the deadline, resign shortly after joining, or get rejected at the document verification stage. To ensure every sanctioned post is filled, IBPS draws candidates from the reserve panel, based on merit, category, and the number of vacancies still open, and provisionally allots them to a Regional Rural Bank for the Office Assistant/Customer Service Associate (Clerk) post.

This section outlines the step-by-step process to view and download your reserve list allotment status.

  1. Visit the official IBPS website at ibps.in.
  2. Click on the "CRP-CSA (Customer Service Associate)" tab on the homepage.

  6. View your allotment status and download the result for future reference.

How Will You Know If You're Selected?

This section explains how IBPS notifies candidates who get provisional allotment through the reserve list.

Candidates who are provisionally allotted a bank through the reserve list will receive an official communication via email and SMS on their registered email ID and mobile number. It is advisable to regularly check your registered contact details and the official IBPS portal so you don't miss any update.

What Happens After the Reserve List Allotment?

This section explains the next stages candidates must complete after receiving a provisional allotment.

Getting your name on the reserve list does not mean final selection it is a provisional allotment that becomes confirmed only after the bank completes verification. The typical process that follows includes:

  • Document Verification: Submission of original certificates and identity proofs for cross-checking.
  • Submission of Required Certificates: Educational, category, and other eligibility-related documents as specified by the allotted bank.
  • Medical Examination: Some banks may require a fitness check before final confirmation.
  • Joining Formalities: Completion of paperwork and reporting to the allotted branch.
  • Induction/Training Process: Orientation and training conducted by the bank before you begin regular duties.

Candidates should keep all original and photocopied documents ready in advance to avoid last-minute issues during verification.

Why Does IBPS Release a Reserve List?

This section explains the broader purpose behind the reserve list mechanism in IBPS recruitment.

A reserve list helps maintain smooth recruitment by ensuring sanctioned vacancies don't remain vacant. It benefits candidates who narrowly missed the initial cut-off by giving them another opportunity, while also helping banks manage manpower requirements efficiently across states and categories.

Vacancy Details

Per the official notification, UPSC has announced a tentative total of 349 Assistant Commandant vacancies across five Central Armed Police Forces. Exact force-wise figures can vary slightly between reports, so candidates should refer to the official notification PDF on upsc.gov.in for the final, force-wise breakup rather than relying on secondary estimates.

  • Border Security Force (BSF)
  • Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF)
  • Central Industrial Security Force (CISF)
  • Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP)
  • Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB)

Selection Process

The UPSC CAPF (ACs) selection process has multiple stages, and candidates must clear each stage to proceed to the next:

  1. Written Examination – Paper I (Objective) and Paper II (Descriptive), held on the same day
  2. Physical Standards Test (PST) and Physical Efficiency Test (PET)
  3. Medical Standards Test
  4. Interview / Personality Test

Exam Pattern

Paper Subject Type Marks Duration
Paper I General Ability and Intelligence Objective 250 2 hours 30 minutes
Paper II General Studies, Essay and Comprehension Descriptive 200 3 hours

Paper II is evaluated only for candidates who secure the minimum qualifying marks in Paper I, as UPSC has specified for this exam pattern.

Required Documents

  • Printed copy of the e-admit card
  • A valid original government-issued photo ID (such as Aadhaar, PAN card, Voter ID, or Driving Licence)
  • Passport-size photographs matching the one uploaded during application

Note: UPSC issues e-admit cards online only no admit card is sent by post or email.

How to Download the UPSC CAPF AC e-Admit Card

  1. Visit the official UPSC website, upsc.gov.in, or the e-Admit Card portal at upsconline.gov.in.
  2. On the homepage, look under "What's New" for "e-Admit Card: Central Armed Police Forces (ACs) Examination, 2026."
  3. Click the link and read the on-screen instructions, then select "Yes" to proceed.
  4. Choose to log in either "By Registration ID" or "By Roll Number."
  5. Enter your Registration ID or Roll Number along with your password/date of birth and the security code.
  6. Click "Submit" to view your admit card.
  7. Download the admit card and take at least two printouts.
  8. Carefully check your name, roll number, exam centre, date, and reporting time for errors.

Important Instructions for Exam Day

  • Reach the examination centre well before the reporting time printed on the admit card.
  • Carry the printed admit card along with a valid original photo ID at every stage of the selection process.
  • Mobile phones, smartwatches, Bluetooth devices, calculators, and other electronic gadgets are not allowed inside the exam hall.
  • Use only black ballpoint pens for OMR-based responses, as instructed by UPSC.
  • Follow all instructions given by invigilators and cooperate with frisking/verification procedures.
  • If you notice any discrepancy on your admit card such as an incorrect name, photo, or exam centre contact UPSC immediately through the contact details printed on the admit card itself; do not wait until exam day.
  • Keep the admit card safe even after the written exam, as it is required again at the PST/PET, medical test, and interview stages.

Exam Pattern and Marking Scheme

How to Download GSSSB Call Letter 2026: Step-by-Step Guide

All candidates belonging to the above cadres can download their online call letter (admit card) from 5:00 PM on 10 July 2026 until 15 minutes before the exam starts, by following these steps:

  1. Step 1: Click on the official call letter link: Click Here
  2. Step 2: On the login page, enter your Advertisement Number, Confirmation Number, Date of Birth (DDMMYYYY), and the captcha/image text shown, then click the Login button.

Important Exam Day Instructions

  • Candidates must reach the exam center by the reporting time (7:30 AM) shown in the call letter. Entry will not be given under any circumstances to candidates arriving after the reporting time.
  • Biometric verification will be carried out for all candidates at the exam center.
  • Candidates must bring a physical printout of the online call letter to the exam center; it is compulsory.
  • Candidates should carefully read all instructions printed on the call letter, since they are also needed for filling attendance sheet details and for the exam process.

Documents Required for Scribe/Compensatory Time Application

Sr. No. Document
1 Copy of the online application form filled by the candidate
2 Photocopy of the candidate's identity proof
3 Proof of disability / temporary disability certificate (APPENDIX-I, issued by a competent authority i.e. Civil Surgeon)
4 Identity proof of the scribe (lahiya)
5 Proof that the scribe's educational qualification is not more than one level below the minimum qualification required for the post
6 Age proof of the scribe (Aadhaar Card / Birth Certificate / SSC mark sheet showing date of birth / School bonafide certificate / School leaving certificate)

Special Category Rule (Blindness, Both-Hand Disability, Cerebral Palsy)

According to the notice, candidates with blindness, disability in both hands, or cerebral palsy are treated differently from other categories. All other disabled candidates, along with candidates with temporary disability due to accidental circumstances who are unable to write or face difficulty writing, must additionally submit a medical certificate as per APPENDIX-I (Certificate regarding physical limitation in an examinee to write) along with supporting evidence, in person or via email, to the Mandal. The Mandal's decision on eligibility for this facility, based on the submitted evidence, is stated to be final.

Duties of the Scribe (Lahiya)

  • The scribe must sit at a distance from the candidate such that the candidate cannot easily touch him/her.
  • During the exam, the scribe must carefully read out the instructions given on the question booklet, OMR answer sheet, or on the computer screen (in case of CBRT), to the candidate.
  • The scribe must read out questions as instructed by the candidate and carefully mark (encode) the answers exactly as the candidate directs.
  • The scribe must inform the candidate about time remaining, as instructed by the candidate.
  • The scribe must not mark any answer on his/her own judgment, must not lead or hint the candidate towards any answer, and must not discuss exam matters with the invigilator or others in the exam hall.
  • If the scribe engages in indiscipline or misconduct in the exam hall, the candidate who availed the scribe's help will be held responsible, and disciplinary action may be taken. The candidate's candidature is liable to be cancelled in such cases.

For all future competitive exams conducted by the Mandal, candidates seeking scribe/compensatory time facility must submit the prescribed form along with self-attested copies of required documents for prior approval, generally at least 5 days before the exam date, or as per the instructions in the relevant advertisement.

CBI Apprentice Vacancy Details 2026

The Central Bank of India has announced a total of 4,500 Apprentice vacancies for the financial year 2026-27, distributed across various states and union territories. Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh reportedly have the largest state-wise allocations. Candidates are advised to refer to the official notification PDF on the bank's recruitment page for the exact state-wise and category-wise vacancy breakup, since detailed figures for every state were not confirmed in the sources reviewed for this article.

Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must meet the educational qualification, age limit, and nationality conditions set by the Central Bank of India to be eligible for the Apprentice post.

Educational Qualification

  • A graduation degree (bachelor's degree) in any discipline from a recognised university or institute.
  • Candidates should have completed graduation on or after 1 January 2022 (some sources indicate the cut-off as 1 January 2021; candidates should verify the exact date on the official notification).
  • Candidates with one year or more of work or training experience after graduation are not eligible, since this scheme is meant for fresh graduates.
  • Candidates who have already completed apprenticeship training, or are currently undergoing apprenticeship training elsewhere, are not eligible.
  • Basic computer knowledge is required.
  • Candidates must be proficient in the local language of the state they are applying for.

Age Limit

Candidates must be between 20 and 28 years of age as on 31 May 2026, meaning they should be born between 31 May 1998 and 31 May 2006 (both dates inclusive).

Category Age Relaxation
OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) 3 years
SC / ST 5 years
PwBD (UR/EWS) 10 years
PwBD (OBC) 13 years
PwBD (SC/ST) 15 years

Candidates should check the official notification for the exact category-wise age relaxation applicable to them.

Salary / Stipend Details

Selected apprentices will receive a fixed monthly stipend of ₹15,000 during the 12-month training period. This is a training stipend rather than a regular salary, and no other allowances or benefits are provided. Completion of the apprenticeship does not guarantee permanent employment with the bank.

Application Fee

The exact application fee amount for the CBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 was not confirmed in the sources reviewed for this article. Candidates should refer to the official Central Bank of India Apprentice notification PDF on centralbank.bank.in for accurate, category-wise fee details, since this cannot be reliably stated here.

Selection Process

The Central Bank of India Apprentice selection process involves two stages:

  1. Online Written Examination: An objective-type computer-based test with no negative marking for wrong answers.
  2. Local Language Proficiency Test: Candidates who qualify the online exam may need to appear for a test assessing reading, writing, and speaking skills in the local language of the applied state. Candidates who studied the local language at Class 10 or Class 12 level may be exempted from this test, subject to document verification.

Final selection also depends on document verification and meeting the required medical fitness standards set by the bank.

Documents Required at the Exam Centre

  • Printed copy of the CBI Apprentice Admit Card 2026
  • A valid original government-issued photo ID proof, such as Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Passport, Voter ID, or Driving Licence
  • A photocopy of the photo ID for verification
  • Recent passport-size photographs, as specified in the admit card instructions

Candidates should ensure the name on their ID proof matches the name printed on the admit card to avoid denial of entry.

How to Download the CBI Apprentice Admit Card 2026

Follow these steps to download your Central Bank of India Apprentice hall ticket:

  1. Visit the official website of the Central Bank of India at centralbankofindia.co.in or centralbank.bank.in.
  2. Go to the "Recruitment" or "Careers" section on the homepage.
  3. Click on the "CBI Apprentice Admit Card 2026" or "Download Call Letter" link.
  4. Enter your Registration Number/Roll Number and Password or Date of Birth.
  5. Fill in the captcha code, if required.
  6. Click the Login or Submit button.
  7. Your CBI Apprentice Hall Ticket 2026 will appear on the screen.
  8. Carefully verify all details, including your name, photograph, signature, exam date, and exam centre.
  9. Download the admit card and take a clear printout on an A4 sheet for the examination.

RBI Grade B Phase 1 Admit Card 2026 - Released

The RBI Grade B Phase 1 call letter was released on 5th June 2026, ahead of the Phase 1 examination held on 13th June 2026. The call letter was made available through the official RBI recruitment portal and candidates were required to log in with their registration credentials to access it. This section also applies to candidates of DEPR and DSIM posts, whose Phase 1 exam was scheduled for 14th June 2026.

The Phase 1 exam is qualifying in nature only scores from this stage are used solely to shortlist candidates for Phase 2 (Mains). Marks from Phase 1 do not contribute to the final merit list.

RBI Grade B Mains Admit Card 2026 - Expected in July

With Phase 1 completed, all attention now turns to the RBI Grade B Phase 2 Mains Admit Card 2026, which is expected to be released in July 2026, ahead of the Mains exam scheduled on 25th July 2026 for General posts and 26th July 2026 for DEPR/DSIM posts. RBI typically releases the Mains hall ticket approximately 7 to 10 days before the exam date, so candidates should watch the official website closely during the second week of July.

The Mains exam is a comprehensive paper that tests a candidate's knowledge of Economic and Social Issues, Finance and Management, and English Writing Skills. Unlike Phase 1, Phase 2 marks are directly counted in the final selection.

 

How to Download RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026

Downloading the RBI Grade B call letter is a straightforward process. The same steps apply for both Phase 1 (already released) and Phase 2 (upcoming). Follow the steps below to access your hall ticket from the official website.

Step 1: Visit the official RBI recruitment portal at https://opportunities.rbi.org.in/

Step 2: Look for the admit card link under the "Call Letter" section select the link for the relevant phase (Phase 1 or Phase 2).

Step 3: A login page will appear on your screen.

Step 4: Enter your Registration Number and Date of Birth / Password in the respective fields.

Step 5: Click on the Submit button. Your RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026 will be displayed on the screen.

Step 6: Carefully verify all the details printed on the call letter name, roll number, exam centre, and shift timing.

Step 7: Download and take at least 2 printouts to carry on exam day.

Step 8: Read all exam day instructions mentioned on the call letter before the examination.

Details to Verify on Your RBI Grade B Call Letter

After downloading the admit card, candidates must cross-check the following details to ensure everything is accurate. If any discrepancy is found, it must be reported to RBI's recruitment authorities immediately.

The call letter will contain the following information:

Candidate's Name, Roll Number and Registration Number, Photograph and Signature, Date of Birth, Category (UR/OBC/SC/ST/EWS/PwBD), Post Applied For, Exam Date and Shift Timing, Reporting Time and Gate Closing Time, Exam Centre Name, Address, and Code, and Important Exam Day Instructions.

Documents to Carry to the RBI Grade B Exam Centre

Carrying the right documents to the examination centre is mandatory. Entry will not be granted if the candidate fails to produce valid identity proof along with the printed admit card.

Every candidate must bring the following on exam day:

Printed copy of the RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026, 2 recent passport-size photographs, one valid original Photo ID proof such as Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Passport, Voter ID, or Driving Licence, and a photocopy of the same Photo ID.

PwBD candidates should additionally refer to the Instructions for PwBD Candidates using Scribe and/or Compensatory Time document available on the official website.

The Phase 1 exam for General posts was conducted on 13th June 2026 in a single shift. Candidates were required to arrive at the exam centre well before the gate closing time. The general shift schedule for the exam is outlined below.

Exam Phase Reporting Time Gate Closing Time Exam Time
Phase 1 1:00 PM 1:45 PM 2:00 PM - 4:00 PM

Note: Individual admit cards may contain slightly different timings based on centre and shift allocation. Always follow the timing printed on your specific call letter.

RBI Grade B Exam Pattern 2026

Understanding the exam pattern helps candidates prepare effectively for both phases of the selection process. The RBI Grade B selection consists of Phase 1 (Prelims), Phase 2 (Mains), and an Interview round.

Phase 1 Exam Pattern - Objective Type (Qualifying)

Phase 1 is a 2-hour online objective exam carrying 200 marks across 200 questions. Since it is only qualifying, candidates must clear it to advance to Mains, but these marks do not count toward the final score.

Section Questions Marks Duration
Reasoning Ability 60 60 45 Minutes
English Language 30 30 25 Minutes
Quantitative Aptitude 30 30 25 Minutes
General Knowledge (GA) 80 80 25 Minutes
Total 200 200 120 Minutes

Phase 2 (Mains) Exam Pattern - Objective + Descriptive

Phase 2 is the main scoring round with 300 marks spread across 3 papers. Both objective and descriptive components are tested. Marks from this stage directly determine the final merit list.

Paper Subject Question Type Marks Duration
Paper I Economic & Social Issues (ESI) Objective + Descriptive 100 120 Minutes
Paper II English (Writing Skills) Descriptive 100 90 Minutes
Paper III Finance & Management (FM) Objective + Descriptive 100 120 Minutes
Total     300 330 Minutes

RBI Grade B Exam Day Instructions 2026

RBI has issued specific instructions that every candidate must follow on exam day. Non-compliance may result in disqualification from the examination.

Candidates must reach the exam centre before the gate closing time without fail. Biometric verification including thumb impression and photograph capture will be conducted at the centre. Ensure your name on the admit card matches exactly with your photo ID. Wearing clothes with metal items, large buttons, or accessories that could trigger security checks should be avoided. Electronic devices including mobile phones, smart watches, Bluetooth devices, calculators, and books are strictly prohibited inside the examination hall. The exam centre and date allotted on the call letter are final no requests for change of centre, date, or session will be entertained.

HPCL Apprentice Educational Qualification and Eligibility

  • Engineering Graduation in Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, or Instrumentation streams, recognized by the Board of Technical Education/UGC/AICTE or equivalent authority.
  • Candidates must have completed their engineering graduation on or after 01-09-2023. Those who completed earlier are not eligible.
  • UR/OBC-NC candidates require 60% aggregate marks; SC/ST/PwBD candidates require 50% aggregate marks, calculated across all semesters/years.
  • Where CGPA/GPA or letter grades are awarded, the percentage must be converted as per the university/institute's norms, supported by a certificate from the university/institute.
  • Only Indian nationals are eligible to apply.
  • Only candidates registered and approved on the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS 2.0) portal and by the Board of Apprenticeship Training (BOAT) will be considered.
  • Candidates with an existing apprenticeship contract with any other organization on the NATS portal are not eligible to apply.
  • Candidates with one year or more of work experience are not eligible to apply.

HPCL Apprentice Monthly Stipend

Selected Graduate Apprentice Trainees (Engineering) will be paid a monthly stipend of Rs. 25,000/-, comprising Rs. 20,500 paid directly by HPCL and Rs. 4,500 paid to apprentices by the Government of India under the DBT scheme. HPCL has no obligation to provide housing assistance or any other allowance beyond this fixed stipend.

HPCL Apprentice Selection Process

  1. Applications are screened based on merit percentage as per eligibility criteria and the number of training slots notified.
  2. Incomplete or ineligible applications are summarily rejected without intimation.
  3. Shortlisted candidates are called for document/certificate verification in a ratio of 1:5 against notified training slots, communicated via registered email. No TA/DA is paid for the verification process.
  4. A merit list is prepared based on candidates who report for verification and are found suitable.
  5. Selected candidates must accept a tri-partite apprenticeship contract on the NATS website and submit a medical certificate and undergo police verification.

HPCL Apprentice Application Fee

Application fee details are not specified in the official notification.

Documents Required for HPCL Apprentice Application

  • Recent passport-sized photograph
  • Signature (for upload)
  • Engineering degree/marksheets for percentage calculation
  • SC/ST/OBC-NC/PwBD certificate in the prescribed format, where applicable (available at www.hpclcareers.com > Downloads > Downloads for Apprentices)
  • Self-certified translated copy of category certificates if issued in a language other than English/Hindi

How to Apply Online for HPCL Apprentice Recruitment 2026

  1. Register on the Apprentice Application portal at jobs.hpcl.co.in/Recruit_New/recruitlogin.jsp using the "Sign up for New Registration" option.
  2. Login credentials will be sent to the registered email ID by the HPCL Apprentice Team.
  3. Sign in using the received email ID and password.
  4. Select the Engineering Branch from the dropdown as per the branches mentioned in the advertisement.
  5. Fill in Personal Details and click "Validate your details."
  6. Click "Save & Next" to proceed to Contact Details, including correspondence and permanent address.
  7. Select State of Training (only one preference can be selected).
  8. Validate details and proceed to Qualification Details.
  9. Upload a recent passport-sized photograph and signature.
  10. Recheck all details under "Preview" and edit if required.
  11. Read the declaration carefully, check the declaration boxes, and click "Final Submit."
  12. A confirmation email with the HPCL Application Number will be sent after submission.

Note: Candidates are allowed to fill only one application; multiple applications will be rejected.

HPCL Apprentice Important Instructions

  • HPCL does not guarantee permanent or temporary employment after successful completion of apprenticeship.
  • Apprentices who complete the training successfully will receive relaxation/preference in future recruitment norms in two stages: age relaxation to the extent of the apprenticeship period (not exceeding one year), and an additional 5% grace marks in the Computer Based Test (CBT) for shortlisting in subsequent recruitment.
  • Furnishing wrong or false information will lead to disqualification, even after engagement.

NCL Recruitment 2026: Selection Process and Exam Pattern

  • Section A: Technical knowledge (discipline-related), 70 MCQs.
  • Section B: General Knowledge, General Awareness, Reasoning, Verbal & Mental Ability, and Quantitative Aptitude, 30 MCQs.

  • The question paper is bilingual (English and Hindi); in case of ambiguity, the English version is valid and final.
  • The CBT will be held at Test Cities as mentioned in the online application form; candidates may opt for their preferred city, which cannot be changed after submission.

NCL Recruitment 2026: Syllabus

Mining Sirdar T&S Gr. C - Section A (70 Marks)

  • Opencast coal mine working; bench formation, dump management, and haul road design
  • Shot firing and transport and use of explosives in mines
  • Safety issues in opencast workings, transport of material, working at heights, marching and deployment of heavy machines
  • Preliminary idea about reclamation operation in opencast mining
  • Preliminary understanding of safety management plan
  • Provisions of the Coal Mines Regulations 2017, Rules and Bye-laws under the Mines Act 1952, relating to safety of persons employed in mines and duties of Sirdars and Shot firers
  • Mines Rules 1955, Mines Vocational Training Rules 1966, Mines Rescue Rules 1985, DGMS Circulars
  • Writing of reports

Mine Surveyor T&S Gr. B - Section A (70 Marks)

  • Linear measurement, chain surveying, optical square
  • EDM: principles, types, correction, and selection of instruments
  • Angular measurement: prismatic compass, bearing of lines, local attraction, magnetic declination
  • Plan table surveying and contouring
  • Miners' dials and other compass instruments
  • Theodolite, traversing, and traverse calculations
  • Total stations: surveying, errors, adjustments, applications
  • Levelling: instruments, types, geometrical, trigonometric and physical levelling, contouring
  • Tachometry
  • Controlled surveys: triangulation, trilateration, GPS and total station applications
  • Field astronomy, Gyro Theodolite, azimuth determination
  • National grid, map projections, geodesy
  • Photogrammetry and remote sensing in mining
  • Theory of errors and adjustments
  • Area and volume calculation, earthwork estimation
  • Borehole surveying, dip, strike, outcrop and fault problems
  • Mine plans, legislation, and duties of surveyors
  • Geological map reading
  • Computer applications in mine surveying, 3D laser profiling
  • Dump/high wall stability monitoring
  • Software knowledge: Surpac, AutoCAD, Liscad, Autoplotter, Riscan Pro
  • Modern survey equipment: 3D Terrestrial Laser Scanner, GPS, Drone

Section B (Common for All Posts, 30 Marks)

  • General Knowledge - India and international relations, General Science
  • General Awareness - Sports, Defense, Books, Prizes, Indian democracy
  • Reasoning, Verbal & Mental Ability - Synonym & Antonym (Hindi/English), Grammar, Relationship
  • Quantitative Aptitude - Work relationship, Profit & Loss, Speed

NCL Recruitment 2026: Documents Required

  • Scanned copy of recent passport-size color photograph (not older than 3 weeks, jpg/jpeg format)
  • Scanned copy of signature in black ink pen (jpg/jpeg format)
  • Scanned copy of Matriculation/Secondary Board level certificate
  • For Mining Sirdar T&S Gr. C: valid Mining Sirdar/Overman's Certificate of Competency issued by DGMS, valid Gas Testing Certificate, valid First Aid Certificate
  • For Surveyor (Mining) T&S Gr. B: valid Surveyor's Certificate of Competency (SCC)
  • For Mining Sirdar T&S Gr. C: scanned copy of Degree/Diploma in Mining Engineering (if applicable)
  • For Surveyor T&S Gr. B: scanned copy of Degree/Diploma in Mining/Mine Surveying Engineering (if applicable)
  • OBC (Non-Creamy Layer)/SC/ST candidates: self-attested valid caste certificate in prescribed format
  • EWS candidates: self-attested valid Income & Asset certificate as per OM No. 36039/1/2019-Estt(Res) dated 31.01.2019, based on FY 2025-2026 gross annual income
  • Self-attested certificate in prescribed format for J&K domicile (if applicable)

NCL Recruitment 2026: How to Apply

  1. Log in to the official NCL website using URL www.nclcil.in > Career > Recruitment > Employment Notification for Direct Recruitment of various Statutory posts > Apply Online.
  2. Read the complete Employment Notification carefully (available in English and Hindi) to assess your eligibility.
  3. Candidates other than SC/ST/Ex-Servicemen/Departmental Candidates must pay a non-refundable application fee of ₹1180/- through the online facility.
  4. Upload the scanned photograph, signature, and all required documents as specified in the notification.
  5. A candidate can apply for only a single post against this Employment Notification.
  6. Verify all details (Date of Birth, Category, Contact Details, Qualifications) carefully before final submission, as no correction is possible after submission.
  7. If more than one application is received from a candidate, the most recent application will be treated as final.
  8. No hard copies of the application or testimonials need to be posted or dispatched to NCL.

Important Instructions

  • A candidate can apply for only one post against this Employment Notification.
  • All qualifications must be recognized by AICTE/UGC/appropriate Indian Statutory Authorities.
  • Mere issuance of Admit Card does not imply that candidature has been finally cleared by NCL; candidature remains provisional until eligibility is verified against original documents after clearing the CBT.
  • No relaxation in minimum educational qualification is admissible for any category of candidate.
  • Where Grade (CGPA/OGPA/DGPA) is awarded, a conversion certificate from the concerned Board/University must be produced at the time of document verification.
  • Candidates employed in Govt./Semi-Govt./PSU/Autonomous Bodies must produce a 'No Objection Certificate' at the time of document verification, if shortlisted, and must resign from their present job before joining NCL upon final selection.
  • Selected candidates could be posted at any NCL Mine/Establishment and are liable to be transferred to other Coal India Limited subsidiaries during service.
  • Appointment is subject to candidates being found medically fit as per CIL's Medical Examination Rules.
  • SC/ST candidates called for CBT will be paid up to IInd Class Non-AC fare as per rules, subject to submitting the TA Claim format with required enclosures.
  • No TA/DA will be paid for appearing in CBT, scrutiny/verification, or joining, except as provided in the notification.
  • Court of Jurisdiction for any dispute will be the Honorable High Court of Jabalpur, M.P.
  • In case of any ambiguity, the English version of the Employment Notification will be considered valid.
  • Candidates must have an active email ID and mobile number valid for at least the next one year, as all correspondence will be through these or the NCL website.

Age relaxation: 5 years for SC/ST candidates, 3 years for OBC-NCL candidates, 10 years for PwBD candidates. Relaxation of age for Ex-Servicemen is as per Government guidelines. Upper age limit for an Ex-Trade Apprentice of AVNL is relaxable by the period of apprenticeship training undergone under the Apprenticeship Act.

AVNL Recruitment 2026: Remuneration

Post Basic Special Allowance (5% of Basic) Medical Insurance, Conveyance & Mobile Charges/Month Total (excl. IDA)
Junior Technician Rs. 21,000 Rs. 1,050 Rs. 3,000 Rs. 25,050 + IDA

Category Application Fee
General / EWS / OBC Rs. 300/- (non-refundable)
SC / ST / PwBD / Ex-Servicemen (XSM) / Female Nil

Fees must be paid online through Net Banking, Debit Card, Credit Card, or UPI. Fees once paid are non-refundable under any circumstances.

AVNL Recruitment 2026: Exam Pattern

The written exam is a single Computer Based Test (CBT), objective multiple-choice type, for a maximum of 100 marks, with no negative marking.

Part Subject Questions Marks
Part A (General Paper) General Awareness 10 10
Part A (General Paper) General English 10 10
Part A (General Paper) Quantitative Aptitude 10 10
Part A (General Paper) Reasoning Ability 10 10
Part A (General Paper) Computer Aptitude 10 10
Part A Total   50 50
Part B (Junior Technician) NCVT syllabus of relevant trade 50 50
Part B (Junior/Assistant/Deputy Manager) Relevant discipline 50 50

Part A questions are up to 10th Standard level for Junior Technician posts, and Graduate level for all other posts. Total time allowed for the written exam is 2 hours. Written exam weightage is 100% for Junior Technician posts and 85% for Junior Manager, Assistant Manager, and Deputy Manager posts. There is no written exam (CBT) for Senior Manager, Deputy General Manager, Additional General Manager, and Consultant posts.

AVNL Recruitment 2026: Selection Process

  • Junior Technician posts: CBT, followed by a qualifying Trade Test (Practical) at the respective AVNL unit. Merit is decided solely on Written Test marks; the Trade Test syllabus is per Annexure-A of the official notification.
  • Junior Manager, Assistant Manager, Deputy Manager posts: CBT, followed by an Interview (50 marks, 15% weightage) assessing technical knowledge, prior work experience, initiative, and decision-making. Merit is decided on combined Written Exam and Interview performance.
  • Senior Manager, Deputy General Manager, Additional General Manager, Consultant posts: No written CBT. Candidates are assessed through Presentation, Experience, Expertise, Knowledge, and Interview, conducted at AVNL CO, Avadi.
  • Candidates qualifying the CBT will be called for Interview (other than Junior Technicians) or Trade Test (Junior Technicians) in a post:candidate ratio of 1:3 in order of merit within each category; the final ratio will be decided by AVNL management based on the number of qualifying candidates.
  • Names of candidates shortlisted for CBT, Interview, or Trade Test, and final selections, will be notified on the AVNL website.

AVNL Recruitment 2026: Test Centres

The CBT will be held at: Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Jabalpur, Nagpur, Pune, Mumbai, New Delhi, Kolkata, and Kanpur. Candidates must indicate their preferred test centre in the online application form. AVNL reserves the right to modify, add, or cancel test centres depending on the number of eligible applicants; affected candidates will be assigned a new centre.

Documents Required for AVNL Recruitment 2026

Personal Documents

  • Class X passing certificate/marksheet, PAN Card, and Aadhaar Card for name and date-of-birth proof (name and DOB must match across all documents)
  • Caste/disability certificate (for SC/ST/OBC-NCL/PwBD/EWS candidates), as applicable
  • Trade Apprentice Training Certificate (for Ex-Trade Apprentices of AVNL)
  • OBC-NCL certificate in central format for the current financial year (FY 2026-27)
  • EWS candidates: current-year Income & Asset certificate (valid for FY 2026-27, based on FY 2025-26 income)
  • Disability certificate as per the latest prescribed central government format, generated via the Swavalamban/UDID portal, clearly indicating type and percentage of disability

Qualification Documents

  • NTC/NAC certificate in the relevant trade issued by NCVT (for Junior Technician posts)
  • Bachelor's Degree (Provisional/Final) Certificate (for all other posts)

How to Apply for AVNL Recruitment 2026

Step 1: Registration

  1. Visit the AVNL website and click the "Careers" tab at avnl.co.in
  2. Go to Career - "Register"
  3. Fill in Post name, Post Code (auto-selected), Name, Mobile Number, and Email ID
  4. Generate OTP, enter Captcha, and submit
  5. Enter the OTP received
  6. Accept Terms & Conditions via the "I Agree" checkbox, then click re-verify
  7. Select the checkboxes confirming entered values are correct, enter Captcha for re-verification, and submit registration details
  8. Receive the Registration Number, Login ID, and Password on the registered Email/Mobile

Step 2: Filling the Application Form & Fee Payment

  1. Click "Go to Application" or log in again with the Login ID and Password
  2. Fill in the complete application form
  3. Upload photograph, signature, and required documents (DOB proof, Proof of Educational Qualification, Category Certificate, Apprenticeship Training Certificate, PwBD/Ex-Servicemen proof, if applicable)
  4. Preview the application form before submission
  5. Edit details if required (Name, Post Applied, Email ID, and Mobile Number cannot be changed once submitted)
  6. Submit the application by clicking "I Agree" and entering the Captcha

Step 3: Fee Payment

  1. Choose the payment mode and proceed to the Payment Gateway
  2. Do not refresh or navigate back during payment
  3. Verify fee details and pay the application fee online
  4. On successful payment confirmation, you will be redirected back to the submitted application form
  5. Download the Application/Registration form for your records

No document is required to be sent to AVNL by post; the downloaded application slip should be retained by the candidate for future reference.

Important Instructions

  • Selection of Option for ALL Units wherever a post is available is mandatory to complete the application.
  • Candidates should necessarily upload all required documents while applying; applications with incomplete or insufficient documents are liable to be rejected.
  • Candidates are advised to apply for one post; in case of a clash in CBT dates, the candidate must choose one post/trade to appear for.
  • The category once filled in the online application form cannot be changed.
  • All computation of age, experience, and qualification requirements will be done with reference to the closing date of online registration.
  • Where a qualifying degree does not mention the required specialization, candidates must submit a certificate from their University/Institution at the time of Interview/Trade Test clearly stating their specialization.
  • Assistive devices/scribes for PwD candidates are allowed at the exam centre, subject to prior permission obtained by emailing [email protected].
  • Any dispute arising from this recruitment can be instituted only in Chennai; courts/tribunals/forums at Chennai have sole and exclusive jurisdiction.
  • AVNL reserves the right to cancel, restrict, curtail, or enlarge the number of vacancies at any time without notice.
  • Selected candidates are subject to verification of educational/technical qualifications, category/disability certificate, experience certificate, and character & antecedents, and must be declared "Medically Fit" by a competent authority.
  • Canvassing in any form will disqualify the candidate.
  • For any issues related to online application submission or fee payment, contact the Help Desk (via the Help Desk tab on the application portal) at 022-61087565, Monday to Friday, 10 AM to 5 PM.

There is no written test — selection is purely merit-based on qualifying marks. Interested and eligible candidates can apply online from 14-07-2026 to 12-08-2026.

Key Eligibility Conditions

  • Candidates must have already passed the prescribed qualification as on the date of reckoning eligibility (31-07-2026); those awaiting results are not eligible.
  • Minimum 50% aggregate marks required (45% for SC and PwBD candidates against seats reserved for them).
  • Only regular full-time courses recognized by the concerned Board/University/Institute/NCVET/SCVT are considered; part-time, correspondence or distance-mode qualifications are not eligible.
  • Diploma/Graduation/ITI must be in the specific branch/subject listed against the respective code; other branches are not considered.
  • Candidates holding higher qualifications such as B.E./B.Tech, MBA, CA, LLB, MCA or equivalent are not eligible.
  • Candidates with one year or more of job experience after acquiring the qualification are not eligible.
  • Candidates who completed the prescribed qualification more than five years before the reckoning date are not eligible.
  • A candidate with B.Sc. (Physics, Mathematics, Chemistry/Industrial Chemistry) may apply for only Code 101 or Code 108, not both. A candidate with B.Com may apply for only Code 108 or Code 109, not both.
  • A candidate can apply for only one Trade/Discipline overall; applying for more than one leads to summary rejection.
  • For Code 108, candidates must choose either Panipat or New Delhi; applying for both locations leads to summary rejection.
  • PwBD candidates can apply only against identified seats under Codes 102, 105, 106, 107, 108, 109, 110 and 111, and must submit a Disability Certificate as per the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules, 2017.

IOCL Panipat Apprentice Recruitment 2026: Stipend

The stipend payable to apprentices shall be as prescribed under the Apprentices Act 1961/1973, Apprentices Rules 1992 (as amended), and IOCL's own guidelines. The exact monthly stipend amount is not specified in the notification.

IOCL Panipat Apprentice Recruitment 2026: Application Fee

The notification does not specify any application fee details. Not specified.

IOCL Panipat Apprentice Recruitment 2026: Selection Process

  • There is no written test for this recruitment.
  • Selection is based on percentage of marks (aggregate of all subjects across all years/semesters) obtained in the prescribed qualification, arranged in descending order, subject to meeting the notified eligibility criteria.
  • Preference is given to candidates applying for apprenticeship training for the first time.
  • In case of a tie in marks, the candidate senior in age (date of birth) is ranked higher; if the date of birth is also the same, higher marks in Matriculation are considered.
  • PwBD candidates who avail relaxation in eligibility qualification marks are considered against reserved seats in order of merit within the category, irrespective of their position in the overall select list.
  • Filling of seats is solely at the discretion of management based on candidate suitability; no claim arises if seats remain unfilled due to insufficient suitable candidates.
  • Shortlisted candidates are called for Document Verification based on merit list position and the number of seats in each Trade/Discipline.

How to Apply for IOCL Panipat Apprentice Recruitment 2026

The application process has two mandatory steps. Both must be completed for the application to be considered valid.

Step I: Registration and Application on NAPS/NATS Portal

  • For Codes 101, 102, 108, 109, 110 and 111: Register on the NAPS portal at https://apprenticeshipindia.gov.in/. Select "Apprenticeship Opportunities," search by location "IOCL, Panipat Refinery & Petrochemical Complex," and select the respective trade, then complete registration and login.
  • For Codes 104, 105, 106 and 107: Register on the NATS portal / Board of Apprenticeship Training (BOAT) at https://nats.education.gov.in. After registration, apply to the IOCL Panipat Refinery & Petrochemical Complex advertisement from the dashboard.

Step II: Filling Additional Details on Microsoft Forms

  2. Submit only one response in the Microsoft Forms.
  3. Ensure the Enrolment No./Student ID/Registration No. and other details match exactly between Step I and Step II.
  4. Use the same email ID and mobile number as registered on the NAPS/NATS portal; both must remain valid for at least the next one year.

IOCL Panipat Apprentice Recruitment 2026: Important Instructions

  • Candidates who have already completed apprenticeship training in a different trade/discipline may apply again, subject to specific gap-period conditions (minimum 1 year gap generally; different conditions apply for employer-side termination, health/financial hardship, or relocation cases). No waiting period applies for women in the hardship-termination case.
  • Candidates whose previous apprenticeship was terminated due to their own failure to fulfil contract terms are not eligible to reapply.
  • The Corporation has no obligation to offer regular employment after completion of apprenticeship, and apprentices cannot claim employment rights on this basis.
  • Furnishing false or incorrect information at any stage will lead to cancellation of candidature and possible criminal prosecution; engagement can also be terminated post-facto if discrepancies are found later.
  • Only those declared medically fit in the pre-engagement medical examination will be considered for engagement.
  • SC/ST/PwBD candidates appearing for Document Verification are reimbursed single second-class railway fare (shortest route, minimum 30 km distance) on production of tickets.
  • No HRA or company accommodation is provided to apprentices.
  • Leave admissible: 32 days General Leave (8 days/quarter, including medical grounds) and 12 days Casual Leave per calendar year (pro-rata); unavailed leave lapses at the end of the apprenticeship period.
  • Apprentices are covered under Accident Insurance and the Certified Standing Orders applicable to workmen at the training establishment.
  • Codes 101, 102, 104, 105, 106 and 107 apprentices are provided one pair of safety shoes and a helmet (returnable on completion of training), wherever applicable.
  • Canvassing in any form will render a candidate ineligible.
  • Candidates are cautioned against fraudulent job offers circulated via email/social media claiming to be from IOCL; only www.iocl.com and Employment News/Press Notifications should be relied upon.

Note: The notification does not mention a specific start or end date for registration on the ICAI Placement Portal. Candidates should regularly check both nabfid.org and the ICAI Placement Portal for updates, since the interview date itself is described as tentative.

NaBFID Business Analyst Vacancy Details 2026

The vacancies are provisional and can be modified or cancelled at the sole discretion of the Bank, without any intimation.

Out of the total vacancies, 3 posts are reserved for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) on a horizontal basis — 1 for Visually Impaired (VI) and 2 for Hearing Impaired (HI) candidates.

Abbreviations: SC – Scheduled Castes, ST – Scheduled Tribes, OBC – Other Backward Classes, EWS – Economically Weaker Section, UR – Unreserved/General, PwBD – Persons with Benchmark Disability, VI – Visually Impaired, HI – Hearing Impaired, LD – Locomotor Disability.

NaBFID Business Analyst Eligibility Criteria 2026

Educational Qualification

The candidate should have cleared the final CA exam as on the cut-off date of 30 June 2026. Only candidates who have registered themselves on the ICAI Placement Portal (icaiplacements.icai.org) as newly qualified Chartered Accountants are eligible.

Reservation-Related Eligibility Notes

  • SC/ST candidates must submit a Caste Certificate issued by a Competent Authority in the Government of India prescribed format, whenever required by the Bank.
  • OBC reservation is available only to 'Non-Creamy Layer' OBC candidates, as governed by Office Memorandum No. 36012/22/93-Estt.(SCT) dated 08.09.1993. 'Creamy layer' OBC candidates must indicate their category as 'General'. The OBC certificate must be in the Government of India prescribed format with the 'Non-creamy layer' clause, issued between 01.04.2026 and the date of interview.
  • EWS reservation is governed by Office Memorandum No. 36039/1/2019-Estt (Res) dated 31.01.2019. EWS vacancies are tentative and subject to further Government of India directives and the outcome of any litigation. EWS candidates must produce an Income & Asset Certificate based on gross annual income for FY 2025-26, valid for 2026-27.
  • Reserved-category candidates for whom no reservation has been mentioned in a particular stream are free to apply under the General category, provided they meet all General category eligibility conditions.
  • There is no reservation for Ex-servicemen in the Officers' Cadre.
  • No change in category is permitted after registration of the online application; no correspondence, email, or phone call will be entertained regarding category change.

PwBD Eligibility

Horizontal reservation is provided to Persons with Benchmark Disabilities as per Section 34 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act (RPwD), 2016. The identified categories for this recruitment are Visual Impairment (VI) and Hearing Impaired (HI):

  • Visual Impairment: Includes blindness (total absence of sight, or visual acuity less than 3/60 in the better eye, or field of vision limited to less than 10 degrees) and low vision (visual acuity not exceeding 6/18 up to 3/60, or field of vision limited to less than 40 degrees up to 10 degrees) after best correction.
  • Hearing Impaired: Hard of Hearing means 60 dB to 70 dB hearing loss in speech frequencies in both ears.

PwBD candidates must produce a certificate issued by a Competent Authority as per Government of India guidelines. Disability conditions classified as "likely to improve" under a temporary category are not eligible for reservation; conditions that are progressive, non-progressive, or not likely to improve are treated as eligible.

Maximum Age (as on 30.06.2026) 32 years

The candidate should not be more than 32 years old as on 30 June 2026. The maximum age indicated is applicable for General/EWS category candidates.

SC/ST 5 years

PwBD 10 years

Important: Cumulative age relaxation is not available, either among the above categories or in combination with any other relaxation item. Candidates must clearly state their reservation status in the application, and copies of relaxation-related certificates must be submitted at the time of interview or joining, in the Government of India prescribed format (if any).

NaBFID Business Analyst Job Profile (Stream-wise)

Lending Operations (Lending & Project Finance)

  • Credit appraisal and financial analysis of lending proposals, including financial statements, business models, cash flow projections, sponsor strength, project risk, security structure, and repayment capacity.
  • Validation of project financial models against the Techno-Economic Viability (TEV) report, industry benchmarks, and regulatory requirements.
  • Coordination on loan documentation, verification of sanction terms and Conditions Precedent (CPs), and initiation of disbursement.
  • ESG monitoring, tracking Early Warning Signals (EWS), and periodic asset quality review.
  • Credit monitoring and portfolio management, including covenant compliance and risk mitigation recommendations.

Investment & Treasury

  • Settlement and accounting of treasury trades, reconciliation and balancing of books, and valuation of securities.
  • Timely submission of regulatory statements, audit reports, and MIS.
  • Exposure to finance and treasury activities including banking, cash and liquidity management, and capital and debt markets.

Accounts

  • Support the Bank's financial reporting, financial planning, and analysis in line with statutory standards.
  • Preparation and analysis of financial statements and management information for strategic decision-making.
  • Financial analysis, budgeting, forecasting, and performance monitoring.
  • Engagement with auditors, tax authorities, and regulators on financial reporting, accounting, and taxation matters.

Risk Management

  • Credit risk assessment of new proposals in line with existing policies and SOPs.
  • Periodic review of the existing portfolio, including internal credit ratings and rating rationale.
  • Monitoring of regulatory and management exposure limits at account and group level.
  • Assistance in determining provisioning requirements and developing/testing internal credit rating models.

Internal Audit

  • Planning, executing, and reporting on Risk Based Internal Audit covering business operations, infrastructure lending/project finance, and support functions.
  • Evaluating internal controls, governance mechanisms, and risk management processes in line with RBI and NaBFID policies.
  • Process walkthroughs, control testing, and preparation of audit reports with findings and recommendations.
  • Support for the Annual Audit Plan and follow-up reviews for audit compliance.

Compliance

  • Design and strengthening of the Bank's Compliance Governance Framework in line with the NaBFID Act and RBI guidelines.
  • Preparing compliance reports, dashboards, and updates for the Board, Audit Committee, and other Board-level committees.
  • Monitoring regulatory circulars and notifications from RBI, FIU-IND, SEBI, CBDT, IRDAI, MCA, and international bodies.
  • Advisory support on AML/CFT, KYC/CDD, sanctions compliance, and beneficial ownership requirements.

Across all streams, candidates should possess excellent communication skills and proficiency in the use of computers and information technology.

NaBFID Business Analyst Application Fee

The notification does not mention any application fee for the Business Analyst post. Candidates apply through registration on the ICAI Placement Portal rather than a direct application to the Bank.

NaBFID Business Analyst Selection Process

  • Selection is entirely through a Personal Interview.
  • NaBFID will shortlist candidates for interview from newly qualified Chartered Accountants registered on the ICAI Placement Portal.
  • Shortlisted candidates will be called for interview in a ratio of 5 to 15 times the position-wise vacancies, as decided by the Bank.
  • Interviews will be conducted only at the Mumbai Centre of ICAI.
  • Total marks for the interview: 100.
  • Minimum qualifying marks: not less than 40% for GEN/EWS candidates, and 35% for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD candidates.
  • The Bank reserves the right to waive or modify the minimum qualifying marks at any stage, without prior intimation.

NaBFID Business Analyst Required Documents

  • Caste Certificate (for SC/ST candidates), in the Government of India prescribed format.
  • OBC Non-Creamy Layer Certificate (for OBC candidates), issued between 01.04.2026 and the date of interview.
  • Income & Asset Certificate for FY 2025-26 (for EWS candidates), valid for 2026-27.
  • PwBD certificate issued by a Competent Authority, as per Government of India guidelines (for PwBD candidates).
  • Relieving letter/discharge certificate in original, for candidates already in service, at the time of joining.
  • No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the employer, for candidates serving in Government/Quasi-Government offices, PSUs, Nationalized Banks, and Financial Institutions, at the time of interview.

How to Apply for NaBFID Business Analyst Recruitment 2026

  1. Register as a newly qualified Chartered Accountant on the ICAI Placement Portal at https://icaiplacements.icai.org.
  2. Regularly check the careers section of the Bank's website, nabfid.org/careers, for updates related to this recruitment.
  3. NaBFID will shortlist candidates directly from the ICAI Placement Portal registrations for the personal interview.
  4. Attend the interview at the Mumbai Centre of ICAI on the notified date, carrying all required original certificates and documents.

Important: No other means or mode of application will be entertained. Hard copies of the application and other documents should not be sent to NaBFID's office. Any application sent directly to NaBFID will not be entertained under any circumstances.

NaBFID Business Analyst Important Instructions

  • The number of vacancies mentioned is provisional and can be modified or cancelled at the sole discretion of the Bank, without intimation.
  • The Bank reserves the right to cancel, restrict, curtail, or enlarge the recruitment process, including the number of vacancies, without further notice or assigning any reason.
  • No correspondence will be entertained from ineligible or non-selected candidates.
  • The Bank's decision on all matters relating to eligibility, selection process, and results is final and binding on candidates.
  • Selected candidates already in service must produce a proper relieving letter/discharge certificate in original from their present employer at the time of joining, failing which they will not be allowed to join.
  • Appointment of a selected candidate is subject to being declared medically fit as per the Bank's requirement.
  • If a candidate is found not to fulfil eligibility norms, or has furnished incorrect/false information or suppressed material facts, their candidature will be cancelled — even after appointment, if detected later, services are liable to be terminated without notice.
  • Any legal proceedings related to this advertisement can be instituted only in Mumbai; courts, tribunals, and forums at Mumbai have sole and exclusive jurisdiction.
  • Instances of incorrect information or process violation detected at any stage will lead to disqualification, including retrospective disqualification if detected after the current selection process, and the candidate will not be allowed to appear in future NaBFID recruitment processes.

UPSC 08/2026 Selection Process

  • Selection is made by the Union Public Service Commission through Recruitment by Selection, which may involve a Recruitment Test (RT) or Combined Recruitment Test (CRT) followed by an interview, or interview only, depending on the post - the notification does not specify which mode applies to each individual post beyond noting that a Recruitment Test may form part of the selection process.
  • Where a Recruitment Test forms part of selection, candidates must clear the minimum level of suitability at both the RT stage and the interview stage for their respective category.
  • The minimum level of suitability in interview, irrespective of whether selection is by interview alone or RT plus interview, is: UR – 50 marks, OBC – 45 marks, SC/ST/PH – 40 marks, out of a total of 100 interview marks.
  • Where the number of applications is large, UPSC may apply shortlisting criteria such as desirable qualifications, higher educational qualifications, higher relevant experience, or a Recruitment Test, to restrict the number of candidates called for interview.
  • Recruitment Test / Combined Recruitment Test, where held, is ordinarily conducted at: Ahmedabad, Bhopal, Chennai, Delhi, Dispur (Guwahati), Jaipur, Jammu, Kochi, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Port Blair, Ranchi, and Visakhapatnam. The list of centres is subject to change and will be notified on the Commission's website.
  • Candidature at every stage remains provisional, subject to the candidate satisfying all prescribed eligibility conditions.

Documents Required for UPSC Advt 08/2026

  • Matriculation/10th Standard certificate or equivalent mark sheet indicating date of birth
  • Degree/Diploma certificate (or provisional certificate with all mark sheets) as proof of educational qualification claimed
  • Order/letter for any equivalent educational qualification claimed, naming the authority and its number/date
  • Experience certificate(s) in the prescribed proforma from the Head of the concerned Organisation/Department, mentioning duration, basic pay/consolidated pay and nature of duties
  • Caste certificate in the prescribed proforma for SC/ST/OBC candidates seeking reservation
  • Non-creamy-layer declaration for OBC candidates, in addition to the OBC certificate
  • Certificate of Disability in the prescribed proforma, issued by a Medical Board constituted by the Central or State Government, for PwBD candidates
  • Documents relating to change of name, if applicable (marriage/divorce/other, as specified in the notification)
  • Age relaxation certificates for Ex-Servicemen, Commissioned Officers, Central/UT Government employees, or other special provisions, as applicable
  • Certificates for any claim of Professional Registration, Language, Publications, NET, GATE, Conference or Internship
  • Declaration by candidates already in regular Government service that they have informed their Head of Office/Department of having applied

Documents such as pay slips, resumes, appointment letters, relieving letters, or unsigned experience certificates must not be uploaded in the Document Upload Module. If any document is in a language other than Hindi or English, an attested/notarised transcript must be submitted.

How to Apply for UPSC Advertisement No. 08/2026

  1. Visit the UPSC Online Application Portal at upsconline.nic.in/ora.
  2. Complete Account Creation on the portal, if not already registered.
  3. Complete the Universal Registration module to generate a Universal Registration Number (URN), which is common across all UPSC recruitments and remains constant for the candidate.
  4. Fill the Common Application Form (CAF), including uploading a photograph and capturing a live photograph as instructed on the portal.
  5. Upload signature: sign three times on plain white paper in black ink and upload the image as per the portal's instructions.
  6. Fill the fourth, post/vacancy-specific module for the desired post, available only during the notified application window.
  7. Upload all supporting documents against each claim (date of birth, category, educational qualification, experience, disability, etc.) as separate PDF files.
  8. Pay the prescribed application fee online, if applicable to your category.
  9. Review all entries carefully - applications cannot be withdrawn, and no correction or alteration is permitted after submission.
  10. Submit the application and download/print the finally submitted Online Recruitment Application for your own records.

Candidates are advised to apply well in advance of the closing date rather than waiting until the last day, and to keep their Aadhaar Card ready as the preferred ID document for verification.

Important Instructions

  • All correspondence from UPSC will be made through the registered e-mail ID only, including interview schedules and requirements for submission of certificate copies - candidates must enter a correct, active e-mail address.
  • Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) can apply for any post listed as "suitable" for their category, even if that specific post is not reserved for PwBD; such candidates are considered by the general standard of merit unless the post carries a PwBD reservation.
  • Only persons with 40% or more of the relevant disability are eligible for the benefit of reservation and other relaxations under PwBD provisions.
  • Where sufficient PwBD candidates are not available for posts exclusively reserved and identified suitable for them, the required years of experience (not the nature of experience) may be relaxed by up to 50%.
  • Scribe facility is available to PwBD candidates in the categories of blindness, both-arms-affected locomotor disability, and cerebral palsy on request; for other categories, a certificate of physical limitation to write from a Government Chief Medical Officer/Civil Surgeon/Medical Superintendent is required.
  • Mobile phones, pagers, programmable devices, storage media, cameras, Bluetooth devices, and similar equipment are strictly banned inside the examination/interview hall, even in switched-off mode.
  • Face authentication is mandatory for all candidates at the examination venue/interview hall.
  • Furnishing false particulars, suppressing material information, tampering with documents, or using unfair means can lead to disqualification and debarment from UPSC examinations and Central Government employment.
  • Canvassing in any form will disqualify a candidate.
  • Summoning for interview does not guarantee selection; appointment orders are issued by the respective Ministry after selection.

📄 Complete Details & Notification

The Indian Army has released the official notification for the 68th Short Service Commission (Technical) Men course, commencing in April 2027. The recruitment is open to unmarried male engineering graduates and final-year engineering students in notified streams. Online applications can be submitted at www.joinindianarmy.nic.in. This article summarizes the eligibility criteria, vacancy details, important dates, selection process, salary structure, and application steps exactly as given in the official notification.

Indian Army SSC Tech 68 Men Vacancy Details (Stream-Wise)

A total of 350 vacancies (tentative, subject to change based on organizational requirements) have been notified across six core engineering streams:

S.No. Core Engineering Stream Vacancies
1 Civil 75
