Common Mistakes to Avoid - SSC SSA UDC Apply Online 2026

Based on the structure and requirements of this departmental exam, candidates must avoid the following errors that commonly lead to rejection or disqualification from the SSC Upper Division Clerk Limited Departmental Exam 2026.

  • Skipping the typewriting test details: The application requires specific information about whether the typewriting test was passed or exempted, including roll number and date. Leaving this blank or providing incorrect details is a common reason for application rejection.
  • Not creating a new OTR on ssc.gov.in: The OTR created on the old website (ssc.nic.in) is not valid on the new SSC website. Trying to log in with old credentials will fail - create a fresh OTR on ssc.gov.in.
  • Missing the departmental forwarding deadline: Submitting the online application on time is not enough. The printed copy must reach SSC (NR), New Delhi by 23 July 2026 through the HoD/HoO. Many candidates miss this step assuming online submission is sufficient.
  • Uploading a pre-existing photograph: The portal only accepts live photographs captured at the time of application. Uploading a pre-taken photo leads to summary rejection of the application.
  • Miniature or blurred signatures: The signature must be clearly visible and occupy at least 80% of the allocated box. Miniature, faded, or rotated signatures are the leading reasons for application rejection.
  • Applying without verifying service eligibility: Candidates must confirm that they have rendered at least five years of approved and continuous service in the LDC/JSA grade as on 01 August 2025 before applying.
  • Name/date of birth mismatch: Details in the application - name, father's name, date of birth - must exactly match the Matriculation certificate. Any discrepancy can cancel candidature.
  • Carrying electronic devices to the exam: Possession of mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, or any electronic gadget in the examination hall attracts a debarment of 3-5 years from all SSC examinations.
  • Changing appearance before the exam: Candidates must ensure their appearance on exam day closely matches the photograph in the application form. Examination staff can deny entry if there is a visible mismatch.

Eligibility Criteria – Who Can Apply for SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025

This is a Limited Departmental Competitive Examination — it is NOT open to the general public. Only serving central government employees who meet specific service and educational conditions are eligible. The crucial date for determining eligibility is 1 August 2025. Candidates who have resigned, quit service, or whose services have been terminated after applying will not be eligible for appointment on the result of this examination.

Service Eligibility Conditions

  • Must be a permanent or regularly appointed temporary Group 'C' employee with Grade Pay of Rs. 1800.
  • Must have rendered not less than 3 years of regular service as a Group 'C' employee with Grade Pay of Rs. 1800 as on the crucial date of 1 August 2025.
  • A Group 'C' employee on deputation to an ex-cadre post with approval of competent authority is also eligible, if otherwise eligible.
  • A Group 'C' employee appointed to an ex-cadre post or another service on transfer who continues to have a lien in the Group 'C' post is also eligible, if otherwise eligible.
  • The parent Service/Cadre of the candidate must be a participating Service/Cadre of this examination.

Educational Qualification

  • Must have passed the 12th standard examination from a recognized Board or equivalent.

Typewriting Test Requirement

Candidates shall have to pass (if not already passed) one of the periodical typewriting tests in English or Hindi held by SSC:

Language Speed on Manual Typewriter Speed on Computer Key Depressions Per Hour (KDPH)
English 30 words per minute (wpm) 35 wpm 10,500 KDPH
Hindi 25 words per minute (wpm) 30 wpm 9,000 KDPH

Note: Candidates who do not pass the typewriting test within the probation period are liable to be reverted. Candidates declared permanently unfit for typewriting by a Civil Surgeon due to physical disability may be exempted in consultation with DoPT.

Disqualification Condition

A candidate who after applying — or after appearing in the examination — resigns, quits service, severs connection, or whose services are terminated will not be eligible for appointment. This rule does not apply to candidates on approved deputation to an ex-cadre post.

Selection Process – SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 Exam Pattern

The SSC JSA LDC LDCE 2025 selection process consists of a single-stage Computer Based Examination (CBE) of 180 marks and 3 hours duration. There is no interview or skill test at the selection stage. Final merit is determined solely on the basis of aggregate performance in the CBE, and the Commission prepares a Select List in order of merit up to the number of vacancies.

Part-I: Computer Based Examination (CBE) – Exam Pattern

Subject Number of Questions Maximum Marks
Comprehension / General English 60 60
General Knowledge 60 60
CSMOP (Central Secretariat Manual of Office Procedure) 60 60
Total 180 180
  • Duration: 3 hours (4 hours for candidates eligible for scribe)
  • Question Type: Objective type, Multiple Choice
  • Negative Marking: 0.25 marks deducted for each wrong answer
  • Medium: Candidates must attempt in the language (English/Hindi) opted in the application form, except the "General English" section which must be attempted in English
  • No Braille Question Paper: There is no Question Paper in Braille for Visually Handicapped candidates
  • Exam Centre: Delhi-NCR only
  • Compensatory Time: 20 minutes per hour for candidates eligible for scribe/assistive devices

Syllabus for Computer Based Examination

Subject Syllabus Content
Comprehension (English/Hindi) and General English Simple composition, Applied Grammar
General Knowledge Current events, everyday observation, general information about India
CSMOP Simple questions from Chapter No. 5, 6, and 10 of the latest CSMOP — Management of Dak Receipts, File Management System, Records Management

Tie-Breaking Rules

When two or more candidates secure equal aggregate marks, the tie is resolved in the following order:

  1. Marks obtained in 'Comprehension and General English' subject of CBE
  2. Marks obtained in 'General Knowledge' subject of CBE
  3. Date of birth — older candidate ranked higher
  4. Alphabetical order of names

Select List Preparation

After the examination, names of finally selected candidates will be arranged by SSC in order of merit. Selected candidates will be recommended for inclusion in the Select List for JSA/LDC Grade of CSCS Cadre up to the required number of vacancies. This is a competitive examination — success does not confer an automatic right to selection unless the cadre authority also confirms suitability based on conduct in service.

SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 Apply Online – Step-by-Step Process

The SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 apply online process is available exclusively at https://ssc.gov.in. This is a two-part process — One-Time Registration (OTR) followed by the Online Application Form. After submission, eligible candidates must also ensure their department forwards the printed hard copy to SSC Northern Region by 23 July 2026. Only applications forwarded by the Head of Department/Head of Office will be considered for admission.

  1. One-Time Registration (OTR) on the NEW SSC website: If you have not yet completed OTR on https://ssc.gov.in, do so first. OTR done on the old website (ssc.nic.in) is NOT valid for the new portal. Keep ready: mobile number, email ID, Aadhaar number (or Voter ID/PAN/Passport/Driving License), and Matriculation (10th class) board/roll number/year of passing. Opt for Aadhaar-Based Authentication for smoother processing. Complete OTR registration within 14 days of starting, or data will be deleted. Save your Registration Number and password.
  2. Log in and apply for the examination: Visit https://ssc.gov.in, log in with your Registration Number and password, click "Apply" under the JSA/LDC LDCE 2025 (CSCS, DoPT) listing in the "Live Exam" section.
  3. Fill the Online Application Form: Personal details (S. No. 1–18) auto-populate from OTR. Fill in cadre (Central Secretariat Clerical Service, DoPT), examination year (2025), joining date of feeder service/cadre, length of service, exam medium (English or Hindi), ministry/department/office details, Head of Department and Head of Office details, and complete service history in chronological order.
  4. Upload photograph (live capture) and signature: Capture a live photograph directly through the application module — no pre-existing photograph is required. Ensure plain background, good lighting, no cap/mask/glasses. Upload scanned signature in JPEG format (10–20 KB), dimensions approx. 6.0 cm (width) × 2.0 cm (height). Blurred or miniature signatures lead to rejection.
  5. Upload required certificates: Upload the following in PDF/JPEG format: (i) Service Book first page certified true copy attested by HoD/HoO; (ii) Certified particulars of service (posts held, pay scale, capacity); (iii) Educational qualification certificate (12th standard or equivalent); (iv) Disability certificate (PwBD candidates only).
  6. Preview, declare, and submit: Use the Preview option to verify all entries. Check photograph and signature compliance. Click "I Agree" on the declaration and submit. On successful submission, take a printout of the application form.
  7. Forward hard copy through department (mandatory): Print the submitted application form and attach self-attested photocopies of supporting documents. Submit to your Head of Department/Head of Office for forwarding to: The Regional Director, Staff Selection Commission (Northern Region), Block No.12, C.G.O. Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi – 110003, so as to reach by 23 July 2026 at 6:00 PM (or 30 July 2026 for candidates abroad/Andaman & Nicobar/Lakshadweep).
  8. Download Admit Card: Admission Certificate (AC) will be uploaded on the SSC-NR website (https://sscnr.nic.in) approximately 10 days before the exam; available for download 3–4 days before the exam. AC will NOT be sent by post.

Important: Only applications forwarded by the Head of Department/Head of Office will be considered. Candidates are advised to submit to their department well before the closing date to ensure timely forwarding. Applications received after the closing date at SSC will be summarily rejected.

Documents Required – Upload Checklist & Hard Copy Submission

Candidates applying for the SSC LDC JSA LDCE 2025 DoPT must upload the following documents at the time of online application and also include self-attested photocopies with the printed application forwarded by the department. All documents must be clear and legible; no original documents should be submitted at this stage.

Documents to Upload Online (and attach with hard copy)

  • Certified true copy of first page of Service Book duly attested by Head of Department/Head of Office — showing name, father's name, husband's name (if applicable), nationality, SC/ST details (if applicable), date of birth in Christian Era (figures and words)
  • Certified particulars of service attested by HoD/HoO — showing posts held, scale of pay, and capacity (substantive/officiating/permanent/temporary)
  • Certificate of essential educational qualification (12th standard or equivalent), if applicable
  • Disability certificate (PwBD candidates) — as per Annexure-VII (Form-V) or Annexure-VIII (Form-VI for multiple disabilities) of the notification

Documents to Carry to Exam Centre

  • Hard copy of Admission Certificate (AC)
  • Departmental Identity Card (Original) issued by employer
  • At least one valid government-issued photo ID — Voter ID, Driving License, PAN Card, Passport, or any Central/State Government-issued photo ID card (for candidates who have not undergone Aadhaar-Based Authentication, also carry two recent passport-size colour photographs and an additional DOB proof)
  • If Photo ID does not show date of birth — carry Matriculation Certificate/Marks Sheet (issued by CBSE/ICSE/State Boards), Birth Certificate, or Category Certificate
  • PwBD candidates availing scribe/assistive devices — carry Medical Certificate (Annexure-II or III) and scribe's photo ID proof (original and photocopy)

Departmental Forwarding Certificate – Role of Head of Department

A unique feature of the SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 is the mandatory role of the Head of Department or Head of Office in the application process. The forwarding authority must certify the candidate's service particulars, verify eligibility, sign and stamp the photograph on the printed application, and forward it to SSC Northern Region by the deadline. Without this forwarding, no application will be considered.

The Head of Department/Office must certify the following key points (as per Annexure-VI of the notification):

  • All information given by the candidate is verified and correct as per service records
  • The candidate belongs to the SC/ST community (if claimed), as verified from service records
  • No circumstance renders the candidate unsuitable for promotion to JSA/LDC of CSCS Cadre, DoPT
  • The candidate is a regularly appointed temporary/permanent Group 'C' employee of the participating Ministry/Department/Organization
  • The candidate fulfills all eligibility conditions for the year 2025 considering the crucial date and length of service
  • The candidate has not been debarred or disqualified by any Public Service Commission/SSC/Subordinate Service Commission for any examination/selection
  • A vacancy in the appropriate category is available in the Department/Organization

Critical: The forwarding authority must also sign the candidate's photograph on the printed application form and put a half-seal on the photograph and half on the form. Without this, the application will be summarily rejected.

PwBD / Scribe Provisions – SSC JSA LDC LDCE 2025

Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) applying for the SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 can avail the facility of scribe, technology, or assistive devices. The eligibility for scribe assistance depends on the nature and percentage of disability. Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour of examination will be provided to all candidates eligible for scribe assistance — whether or not they actually avail the facility.

  • Blindness and Cerebral Palsy (40%+): Scribe/technology/assistive devices provided on request in the application form, with upload of disability certificate.
  • Other PwBD categories: Scribe provided on production of a certificate from Chief Medical Officer/Civil Surgeon/Medical Superintendent of a Government health institution (as per Annexure-II) confirming physical limitation to write.
  • PwD with less than 40% disability having difficulty writing: Scribe provided as per OM No. 29-6/2019-DD-III dated 10.08.2022, on production of certificate as per Annexure-III.
  • Scribe/assistive device facility must be opted for in the online application form — it will not be provided without prior intimation.

Common Mistakes to Avoid – SSC JSA LDC LDCE 2025 DoPT Application

This is a departmental exam with additional procedural requirements not seen in open competitive exams. Many candidates lose their application due to easily avoidable errors. Here are the most critical mistakes to watch for in the SSC JSA LDC CSCS DoPT LDCE 2025:

  1. Using old SSC website OTR for the new website: OTR generated on the old website (ssc.nic.in) is NOT valid on the new website (ssc.gov.in). Candidates must generate a fresh OTR on the new portal. Using old OTR credentials leads to failure to apply.
  2. Not completing OTR within 14 days: If you start OTR registration but do not complete it within 14 days, your data is automatically deleted. Start and complete OTR well before the application deadline.
  3. Submitting multiple applications: Only ONE application should be submitted. Multiple applications may lead to rejection of the entire candidature.
  4. Not ensuring the department forwards the hard copy on time: Many candidates submit the online application correctly but forget that the department must also forward the printed hard copy to SSC NR by 23 July 2026. Applications received late at SSC — even with valid online submissions — are summarily rejected. Inform your department immediately after applying online.
  5. Forwarding authority not signing the photograph: The Head of Department/Office must personally sign the candidate's photo on the printed application form and put a half-seal across the photo. Without this, the application is summarily rejected — no appeal entertained.
  6. Uploading a photograph of a pre-existing photograph: The application module captures a live photograph. Candidates who photograph a pre-existing printed photo (instead of taking a live capture) will have their applications rejected summarily.
  7. Wearing glasses, cap, or mask in the live photograph: Candidates are specifically instructed not to wear any of these while capturing the live photo. Similarly, the appearance at the exam should match the application photo — changed appearances may deny entry.
  8. Uploading a miniature or blurred signature: The signature must be in JPEG format (10–20 KB), approximately 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm, occupying at least 80% of the signature box. Miniature or blurred signatures are a leading cause of application rejection.
  9. Not indicating the correct medium of examination: Candidates must choose English or Hindi as the medium in the application. The General English section must be attempted in English regardless of medium chosen. This choice cannot be changed after submission.
  10. Changing appearance significantly between application and exam day: Since the exam centre staff verifies appearance against the application photo, significant changes (beard, haircut, spectacles) may raise suspicion and lead to not being allowed to appear.

Educational Qualification

Qualification Option Details
Option 1 12th Pass (Intermediate / Senior Secondary)

Age Limit

Salary / Remuneration – CSC Aadhaar Supervisor Operator 2026

Selected candidates under the CSC Aadhaar Operator Recruitment 2026 will be paid as per the state government's prescribed wage structure. The remuneration for all selected Aadhaar Supervisor/Operator candidates will be the minimum wages of the respective state set for semi-skilled manpower. The exact figure will vary from state to state based on the applicable minimum wage notification of Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, or Maharashtra.

How to Obtain the Aadhaar Supervisor Certificate Before Applying

Candidates who do not yet hold the mandatory Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor certificate need to complete two steps before they are eligible to apply for CSC Aadhaar Seva Kendra jobs. First, they must apply for and pass the Aadhaar Supervisor exam; second, they must complete the LMS certification. Both processes are managed through official UIDAI platforms.

  1. Visit the Aadhaar Supervisor exam portal at https://uidai.dexitglobalexams.com/UIDAI/LoginAction.action and submit your exam application.
  2. An authorization request will be sent to the State Team. Once approved, you will be permitted to appear for the Aadhaar Supervisor exam.
  3. After your LMS ID and Password are created and approved, appear for the Aadhaar LMS Certification through the portal at https://e-learning.uidai.gov.in
  4. Once certified, proceed to apply for the CSC Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor district post on the CSC Job Portal.

How to Apply for CSC Aadhaar Supervisor Operator Recruitment 2026

The CSC Aadhaar Operator Apply Online 2026 process is conducted entirely through the official CSC Job Portal at career.csccloud.in. Candidates must ensure they have their Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor certificate ready before beginning the application. The last date to apply is 20 August 2026, and no offline applications are accepted under this recruitment.

  1. Visit the official CSC Job Portal at career.csccloud.in.
  2. Navigate to the relevant job post for your state – Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, or Maharashtra.
  3. Click on the "Apply Now" button on the job post page.
  4. Fill in the online application form with your personal, educational, and certification details.
  5. Upload the required documents including your Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor certificate.
  6. Submit the application form before 20 August 2026.

CSC Aadhaar Supervisor Operator Apply Online 2026

Eligible candidates can submit their online applications for the CSC Aadhaar Seva Kendra Recruitment 2026 through the official CSC Job Portal. The apply online facility is available for all four states – Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra. Ensure your Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor certificate is valid and issued by a UIDAI-authorized agency before clicking Apply Now. The online application window closes on 20 August 2026.

Bihar Apply Now – Bihar
Chhattisgarh Apply Now – Chhattisgarh

Common Mistakes to Avoid in CSC Aadhaar Operator Recruitment 2026

Many candidates make avoidable errors while applying for the CSC Aadhaar Supervisor Operator Vacancy 2026 that can lead to rejection of their application. The points below are based on common patterns seen in similar contractual government recruitment drives and are not derived from the official notification.

  1. Applying without a valid UIDAI certificate: The Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor certificate from a UIDAI-authorized agency is a mandatory requirement. Applying without it will result in disqualification.
  2. VLEs applying despite ineligibility: VLEs are explicitly barred from applying. Submitting an application as a VLE wastes your time and will be rejected at the verification stage.
  3. Applying for the wrong district: Each vacancy is district-specific. Ensure you apply for the correct district as per your location and preference.
  4. Incomplete LMS Certification: Candidates sometimes have the Supervisor exam cleared but not the LMS Certification. Both are required before applying.
  5. Submitting incorrect documents: Upload clear, legible scans of your educational certificates and Aadhaar Operator certificate. Blurry or mismatched documents can cause rejection.
  6. Missing the last date: The portal closes applications on 20 August 2026. Do not wait until the last day — technical issues near the deadline are common.
  7. Confusing CSC e-Governance with state government jobs: This is a contractual, not permanent government post. Ensure you understand the terms of engagement before applying.

IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026-27 Eligibility Criteria

Candidates applying for IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026-27 must be Citizens of India. Merely applying, being shortlisted, or appearing for document verification and personal interaction does not guarantee an offer of engagement in the Bank.

Educational Qualification

Candidates must hold a Degree (Graduation) in any discipline from a University recognized by the Government of India, or an equivalent qualification recognized by the Central Government. The result must be declared on or before 31.07.2026. Candidates registered under the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) must have had their graduation result declared between 01.03.2022 and 31.07.2026, both dates inclusive, and must produce mark sheets and provisional or degree certificates when required.

Age Limit

The minimum age is 20 years and the maximum age is 28 years as on the cut-off date of 01.07.2026 for General and EWS category candidates, meaning the date of birth should fall between 01.07.1998 and 01.07.2006, both dates inclusive. Candidates registered under NAPS should be less than 34 years as on the cut-off date, after applicable relaxation.

Category Age Relaxation
Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe 5 years
Other Backward Classes (Non-Creamy Layer) 3 years
Persons with Benchmark Disabilities 10 years

Age relaxation for SC/ST/OBC candidates is allowed on a cumulative basis with only one of the remaining categories of relaxation. To claim age relaxation, candidates must submit the requisite certificate at the time of personal interaction along with original certificates.

IOB Apprentice Selection Process 2026-27

Selection for IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026-27 will be based on an online examination, a test of the local language wherever applicable, and personal interaction if decided by the Bank. Satisfying the eligibility criteria alone does not guarantee a call for the online examination.

The examination will be conducted online using the candidate's own front camera-enabled desktop, laptop, tablet, or smartphone, and candidates must display the same ID proof uploaded on the apprenticeship portal. Candidates must score a minimum aggregate percentage as decided by the Bank, with a 5 percent relaxation available for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD candidates. There is no minimum qualifying mark for individual subjects.

Test of Local Language

Candidates applying for a particular state must be proficient in reading, writing, speaking, and understanding at least one local language of that state. This test is conducted during document verification after qualifying the written examination. Candidates who have studied the specified local language up to 10th or 12th standard are exempted from this test.

Wait-list

A state-category-wise waitlist will be maintained for one year from the date of the result or the next engagement exercise, whichever is earlier.

How to Apply for IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026-27

Candidates can apply online for IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026-27 from 07.07.2026 to 20.07.2026 by following the steps below.

  1. Register on the NATS portal at https://nats.education.gov.in or the NAPS portal at https://www.apprenticeshipindia.gov.in before applying.
  2. Visit the "Career Opportunities" page on www.bfsissc.com or https://beep.bfsissc.com.
  3. NATS-registered candidates should log in at https://nats.education.gov.in/student_type.php and apply under "Apply against advertised vacancies" for Indian Overseas Bank.
  4. NAPS-registered candidates should visit https://www.apprenticeshipindia.gov.in/apprenticeship/opportunity, search "Indian Overseas Bank," click "View," and then "Apply for this Opportunity."
  5. Provide the NATS/NAPS enrolment number while filling the online application form.
  6. Apply for engagement from only one State/UT, preferably the home State/UT.
  7. Pay the requisite application fee/intimation charges online between 07.07.2026 and 22.07.2026.

No other mode of application or payment will be accepted. Applications once submitted cannot be withdrawn, and fees once paid will not be refunded under any circumstances.

Important Instructions for IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026-27

  • Candidates should not have undergone apprenticeship earlier with IOB or any other organization, or been terminated from apprenticeship training due to their own fault.
  • Candidates with one year or more of training or job experience after completing the educational qualification are not eligible.
  • Apprentices are not treated as "employees" of the Bank and are not entitled to employee benefits.
  • Apprentices are entitled to one day of casual leave per month, totaling 12 days per year, with a maximum of 4 days availed at a time.
  • No Ex-servicemen or Disabled Ex-servicemen shall be engaged as apprentices, and there is no reservation for them in this process.
  • The Bank has no obligation to offer regular employment during or after the apprenticeship period.
  • Furnishing false, incorrect, or tampered information will lead to disqualification or termination, even after engagement.
  • Any request for change of address, email ID, or document verification dates will not be entertained.
  • Any dispute arising out of this recruitment is subject to the sole jurisdiction of courts situated at Chennai.

Law Officer and Rajbhasha Adhikari have a similar structure but include General Awareness with Special Reference to Banking Industry in place of Quantitative Aptitude.

There is a penalty of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer in objective tests; no penalty applies for unattempted questions.

Bank of India Credit Officer Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

Selection for the BOI Credit Officer Bharti 2026 will be through an Online Examination and/or Personal Interview, depending on the number of applicants. If both stages are conducted, the weightage will be 70:30 between the Online Examination and Interview.

  1. Scrutiny of Eligibility: Shortlisting based on documents uploaded at registration.
  2. Online Examination: 125 marks total - English Language (25 marks, qualifying nature) and Professional Knowledge (100 marks), composite duration of 120 minutes.
  3. Personal Interview: 100 marks, conducted for candidates shortlisted based on merit.
  4. Final Merit List: Prepared based on combined scores of Online Examination and Interview.

The minimum qualifying marks in each test is 35% for General/EWS candidates, with a 5% relaxation for SC/ST/OBC/PWD candidates. There is a penalty of one-fourth marks for each wrong answer in the objective test.

When Is the Central Bank of India Apprentice Exam 2026?

Candidates who registered for this recruitment drive want a direct answer to one question: when exactly is the exam? According to the bank's official notification, the written examination for the Engagement of Apprentices under the Apprentices Act, 1961, for FY 2026-27 will be conducted on 5 July 2026, which falls on a Sunday. The exam will be conducted by the BFSI Sector Skill Council (BFSI SSC), the designated agency responsible for administering the test on behalf of Central Bank of India.

This confirms and follows up on the bank's earlier notification dated 11 June 2026, in which applications were first invited for the apprentice engagement process.

Selection Process for Central Bank of India Apprentice 2026

Knowing the full selection process helps candidates prepare for each stage that follows the written exam. Central Bank of India follows a multi-stage selection procedure for apprentice engagement.

The selection process consists of the following stages:

  1. Written Examination - conducted by BFSI SSC on 5 July 2026

  3. Document Verification - verification of educational and identity documents

RBI Site Engineer Selection Process 2026

Candidates wondering about the RBI Site Engineer selection process can note that there is no written exam for this recruitment. Selection happens through preliminary screening by a Screening Committee, followed by document verification and a personal interview.

Step-by-Step Selection Methodology

  • Screening & Shortlisting: The Screening Committee may enhance minimum qualification or experience criteria to limit the number of candidates called, in proportion to the number of vacancies. Merely meeting minimum eligibility does not guarantee an interview call.
  • Interview Call Letter: Shortlisted candidates receive their call letter only via email from [email protected] — no postal call letters are issued.
  • Document Verification: Candidates must produce up-to-date Experience Certificates clearly stating nature of duties, dates, duration, level/position, and responsibilities, along with category, age, and qualification proofs.
  • Interview: Candidates discuss their anticipated compensation (within the advertised range) along with previous employer compensation details before the interview, which is considered by the Selection Committee.
  • Final Selection: The RBI Services Board's decision on eligibility, shortlisting, and interview results is final and binding, with no further correspondence entertained.

  • Left thumb impression (20-50KB) and handwritten declaration in English (50-100KB)

OBC candidates must specifically produce a Non-Creamy Layer certificate based on income for FY 2023-24, 2024-25, or 2025-26, issued on or after 01 April 2026 but before the closing date of 20 July 2026.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying for RBI Site Engineer 2026

Many candidates risk rejection due to avoidable errors during the RBI Site Engineer online application process. Reviewing these common mistakes beforehand can help ensure your application is processed without issues.

  • Writing the declaration in capital letters or another language: The handwritten declaration must be in English, in the candidate's own handwriting, and not in capital letters — non-compliant declarations make the application invalid.
  • Expecting age relaxation: Unlike many government recruitments, RBI has explicitly stated no age relaxation is available for any category in this notification, so candidates must meet the 40-65 year window strictly.
  • Submitting multiple incomplete applications: If multiple applications are filed for the same post, only the last completed one with the higher Registration ID is considered, and the fee from the earlier RID is not adjusted.
  • Uploading documents in the wrong format: Photograph and signature must be JPG/JPEG, while all other supporting documents must be in PDF format within the specified size limits.
  • Not informing current employer: Government/PSU employees must submit an undertaking confirming they have informed their employer in writing about applying, or their candidature may be rejected.
  • Ignoring OBC NCL certificate dating: OBC candidates need a Non-Creamy Layer certificate issued on or after 01 April 2026 — older certificates based on different financial years won't be accepted.

SBI BMO Selection Process 2026

The selection process for the SBI Bank Medical Officer post involves three stages - an Online Written Test, an Interview, and a Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT) - with the final merit list based on 70% weightage to the written test and 30% to the interview. Candidates wondering how marks are normalized can note that the Bank combines scores from both stages using this 70:30 ratio before preparing the final merit list, circle-wise and category-wise.

  1. Online Written Test – Tentatively scheduled for August 2026 across multiple centres nationwide; call letters will be issued via the Bank's website, SMS, and email.
  2. Shortlisting – Based on Professional Knowledge cut-off marks, plus minimum qualifying marks in General Aptitude sections.
  3. Interview – Carries 100 marks; conducted for a category-wise adequate number of shortlisted candidates.
  4. Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT) – Conducted for provisionally selected candidates before joining; candidates with 10th/12th mark sheets showing the relevant local language as a subject are exempted.
  5. Final Result & Wait List – A circle-wise and category-wise wait list valid for one year (or until a fresh advertisement, whichever is earlier) is maintained for non-joining or termination cases.

  1. Visit https://sbi.bank.in/web/careers/current-openings.
  2. Locate and click on Advertisement No. CRPD/SCO/2026-27/03.
  3. Download and carefully read the detailed advertisement.
  4. Click on the "Apply Online" link and register with basic details to generate a provisional registration number and password.
  5. Fill in the application form (editable up to 3 times before final submission).
  6. Upload scanned photograph, signature, and a live photo capture via webcam or mobile.
  7. Upload all required documents in PDF format (each up to 500 KB).
  8. Pay the application fee via Debit Card/Credit Card/Internet Banking.
  9. Submit the form and print/save the system-generated application and e-receipt for future reference.

SBI BMO Recruitment 2026 Apply Online

The direct apply-online link for SBI Bank Medical Officer Recruitment 2026 is available on the Bank's careers page at https://sbi.bank.in/web/careers/current-openings, where candidates must search for Advertisement No. CRPD/SCO/2026-27/03 before proceeding. Applications submitted after 14 July 2026 will not be accepted under any circumstances, so candidates are advised to apply well ahead of the deadline to avoid last-minute website traffic issues.

SBI BMO Recruitment 2026 -  Apply Here

SBI BMO Salary 2026: Pay Scale & Perks

Selected candidates will be placed in the Middle Management Grade Scale-II (MMGS-II) with a basic pay structure of ₹64,820-2340/1-67,160-2680/10-93,960. In addition to basic pay, officers receive DA, HRA, CCA, Provident Fund, NPS contribution, Leave Fare Concession (LFC), and medical facilities as per Bank rules.

  • Non-Practicing Allowance (NPA): 20% of Basic Pay.
  • Higher Start: One increment for a postgraduate diploma; two increments for MD/MS or equivalent.
  • Private Practice: Not permitted for BMOs.
  • Conference Allowance: One local and one national medical conference may be permitted, subject to approval.

Documents Required for SBI BMO Application

Candidates must upload the following documents in PDF format (each up to 500 KB) at the time of application: recent photograph, signature, brief resume, ID proof, date-of-birth proof, educational mark-sheets/degree certificates, NMC/State Medical Council registration proof, experience certificates, caste/EWS certificate (if applicable), PwBD certificate (if applicable), preferred qualification certificates, and Form-16/offer letter/latest salary slip from the current employer.

Troubleshooting & Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying

Many candidates lose out on the SBI BMO opportunity due to avoidable errors rather than ineligibility, so being aware of these common pitfalls can save your application from rejection.

  • Don't wait till the last day (14 July 2026) to register - heavy website traffic near the deadline frequently causes login failures and incomplete submissions.
  • Double-check your Circle/Office choice before final submission - you can apply for only one Circle, and switching later is not permitted.
  • Verify photo and signature specifications carefully (photograph: 20–50 KB, 200×230 pixels; signature: 10–20 KB, 140×60 pixels) to avoid application rejection due to unclear images.
  • Count only post-internship experience - internship, teaching, and training experience do not qualify toward the 5-year (MBBS) or 3-year (PG) experience requirement.
  • Keep your OBC non-creamy layer certificate dated correctly - it must be issued between 01.04.2026 and the date of interview; older certificates will not be accepted.
  • Don't submit multiple applications - only your last completed application is considered valid, and fees paid for earlier attempts are forfeited.
  • Ensure your mobile number and email remain active until the final result is declared, since all call letters and updates are sent only electronically.

How to Check RRB Group D Result 2026

This section walks candidates through the exact steps to access and download their individual result and scorecard from the official RRB portal.

Candidates can follow these steps to check their RRB Group D Result 2026:

The RRB Group D Result 2026 is published individually by each of the 21 RRB zones on their respective regional websites, rather than through a single centralized portal. PET Standards for Male Candidates

What Is the RRB NTPC CBTST Result 2025-26?

The CBTST (Computer Based Typing Skill Test) is a qualifying stage specifically for Category 4 and Category 5 NTPC Graduate posts, which require typing skills. RRB Jammu-Srinagar has now shortlisted additional candidates for all posts, including Category 4 and 5, based on their CBT-2 marks and their qualifying status in CBTST  not on CBTST marks or merit ranking. Roll numbers in the official list are arranged in ascending order, not by merit.

Is this the same as the RRB NTPC Category 1, 2, 3 Final Result?

No. This CBTST-based shortlisting for Category 4 & 5 is a separate exercise from the Category 1, 2, and 3 result (based on CBT-2 and CBAT) that RRB zones released earlier, around May 2026. Candidates should always cross-check their exact roll number against the official PDF on the RRB Jammu-Srinagar website, as this list is meant for quick reference only.

How to Check RRB NTPC CBTST Result 2025-26?

  1. Visit the official result/scorecard login link: rrbapply.gov.in/.
  2. Enter your Registration Number and Date of Birth.
  3. Submit to view your CBTST qualifying status and score card.
  4. Download and save the score card, as it will remain live for only 15 days from activation.

What After RRB NTPC CBTST Result 2025-26?

Candidates shortlisted in this list will now go through Document Verification (DV) followed by Medical Examination.

What happens during RRB NTPC Document Verification?

  • Candidates will be scheduled for DV and notified via email/SMS/website with an e-call letter containing date, time, and reporting venue.
  • Original documents plus two self-attested photocopy sets (A4 size) must be carried, as detailed in the CEN and e-call letter.
  • Scanned true-colour copies of all required documents, photo, and signature must be uploaded through the DV portal: oirms-ir.gov.in/rrbdv. This link becomes active as per a separately issued DV notice.
  • All certificates must be in the prescribed format, in English or Hindi only.
  • No extra time will be given for candidates who fail to bring original certificates on the DV date.
  • Candidates absent during DV or Medical Examination will forfeit their candidature.

What happens during the Medical Examination?

  • Candidates are sent to a nominated Railway Hospital, generally on the day after DV, within the RRB's jurisdiction.
  • Candidates must pay a prescribed medical fee of Rs. 24 only; no other charges apply to the hospital/health unit.
  • For rare additional investigations (CT scan, ultrasound, refractive eye surgery tests) not available at the Railway Hospital, candidates may need to pay the concerned laboratory/hospital directly.
  • Candidates should prepare to be available for 3 to 4 days, covering both DV and medical examination, including travel to the hospital city.

Important Instructions for RRB NTPC CBTST Shortlisted Candidates

  • Shortlisting for DV is purely provisional and can be cancelled at any stage if any inconsistency is found in the candidate's online application data, or if any irregularity comes to RRB's notice.
  • Being called for DV does not guarantee appointment in the Railways.
  • The final select list depends on merit, post preference, medical fitness, and vacancy availability at the time of panel preparation. The final cut-off may go up or down after DV and medical examination.
  • RRB reserves the right to correct any inadvertent error or printing mistake in the shortlisted candidates' list.
  • RRB will not entertain correspondence from unsuccessful candidates.
  • Candidates are advised to be cautious of touts making false promises of selection through illegal means. The RRB selection process is fully computerised and merit-based.

Understanding Your Application Status

A Provisionally Accepted status means the candidate's application meets the eligibility criteria based on the details submitted. What does Conditionally Accepted mean?

A Conditionally Accepted status means the application has been accepted subject to certain conditions specified by the RRB. Candidates should read the conditions carefully and take necessary action if required.

A Rejected status is shown along with the specific reason for rejection, such as incomplete details, document mismatch, or non-fulfilment of eligibility conditions. Candidates are advised to review the reason mentioned on their status page.

How to Download the OSSC CGL Mains Answer Key

OSSC has not yet activated the Mains answer key link. Based on the process the Commission followed for the Prelims answer key, candidates can expect a similar login-based download process once the Mains key is released:

  1. Visit the official OSSC website at www.ossc.gov.in.

  5. The answer key and/or response sheet will open, typically in PDF format.
  6. Download and save it for future reference.

Candidates should also keep the candidate login portal linked in their admit card handy, since OSSC has used a dedicated exam-portal login page for response sheet access in this recruitment cycle. OSSC has not yet issued a separate notice on the Mains objection process. For the Prelims stage, the Commission followed this process, which may be repeated for Mains once the provisional key is out:

  • Select the specific question(s) you wish to challenge.
  • Upload supporting documents or proof, if required.
  • Pay the objection fee, if applicable this is generally refunded if the objection is accepted.
  • Submit the objection within the window specified in the official notice; objections after the deadline are not considered.

The exact objection dates and fee (if any) for the Mains answer key will only be confirmed once OSSC releases the provisional key and accompanying notice.

What Happens After the Mains Answer Key

  • Final Answer Key: Released after OSSC reviews all valid objections.
  • Result Declaration: Prepared using the final answer key; qualified candidates are called for Document/Certificate Verification.

Also Read: UPSSSC Teacher Cadre JTC Answer Key 2026

How to Raise an Objection Against the CG Police SI/Subedar Answer Key

CGPSC has laid out an 11-step process for submitting online claims/objections against the model answer key. Follow these steps exactly as mentioned in the official notice:

  1. Go to the link available on the CGPSC website and log in to raise an online objection against the model answer.
  2. In the candidate Dashboard, go to the Activity Section and click on Objection Filing. A new page will open where you must select the exam name, question paper, set, and question number, and then select the type of objection.
  3. Choose the type of objection from the following options:
    • All Answer Options for the question are incorrect
    • Answer Option issued by the Commission is incorrect
    • More than one Answer Option is correct
    • Question is wrong
    • Question is out of syllabus
    • There is a factual difference in the Hindi and English translation of the question
  4. After selecting the objection type, clearly mention the reason for the objection in the given box, and upload supporting proof as a question-wise PDF file (maximum size 1 MB per question). If any document is downloaded from a web link, it must also be attached as instructed. Objections supported only by a source name/title/link without the actual document attached will not be considered valid. If a book, newspaper, or magazine is used as proof, you must also mention the author's name, edition/publication date, and the relevant reference page number(s).
  5. Use the Add button to submit more than one objection at a time. Wrongly added objections can be removed. All entered objections will be displayed at the bottom of the page, and the Save button must be used to submit them online.
  6. After submitting objections, you will be redirected to the fee payment page, where you can pay the total objection fee for all your objections using the Pay Now button.
  7. After completing all objections and the fee payment, you will receive a payment receipt. You can download and print the question-wise acknowledgement later from Dashboard > Activity Section > Download Acknowledgement.
  8. Once fee payment is successful, the online objection process is treated as complete, and you will not be able to submit objections again.

Objection Fee

Candidates must pay Rs. 50 per question as the claim/objection fee. The fee must be paid online through a bank, by the candidate themselves. If the bank charges any additional service fee during payment, that cost must also be borne by the candidate. Candidates are advised to protect themselves from phishing, hacking, or any other cyber activity while making the online payment.

Also Read: RBI Officer Grade B Phase I Result With Marks 2026

Documents Required for Filing an Objection

  • A question-wise proof document in PDF format (maximum 1 MB per question).
  • If citing a book, newspaper, or magazine as proof: the name of the publication/website link, author's name, edition or publication date, and reference page number(s).
  • Any document downloaded from a web link must be attached only mentioning the source name or link without the document is not valid.

Important Instructions

  • Objections can be submitted online only; no offline application or document will be accepted at the CGPSC office.
  • Candidates get only one opportunity to submit all their objections together for every question they wish to object to. Once the fee is paid, the process is final and cannot be repeated.
  • If the fee payment is unsuccessful, or if a candidate enters different question paper sets within the same paper, or fails to follow the prescribed online objection instructions, the objection will be automatically rejected, and no related application or representation will be considered valid by the Commission.
  • No offline application or document related to the claim/objection will be accepted at the Commission office under any circumstances.

  5. Submit the form in person at the JKSSB office within the objection window.

  • JKSSB, Muthi, Akhnoor Road, Jammu
  • JKSSB, Zamzam Building, Rambagh, Srinagar

RRB JE CBT-2 Answer Key: How to Raise Objections

Candidates who find a discrepancy in the provisional answer key can challenge it during the objection window using the same login portal.

  1. Visit the regional RRB login portal and sign in with your Registration Number and Password.

How to Calculate Your Expected CBT-2 Score

  1. Download the official RRB JE CBT-2 Answer Key 2026.
  2. Compare each of your responses with the correct answer shown in the key.
  3. Award 1 mark for every correct answer.
  4. Deduct 1/3 mark for every incorrect answer.
  5. Add up the marks to arrive at your total probable score.

Formula: Expected Score = Correct Answers - (Wrong Answers × 1/3)

For example, if a candidate has 120 correct answers and 15 wrong answers:
Expected Score = 120 - (15 × 1/3) = 115 marks

OSSSC CRE Prelims Marking Scheme 2026

Before calculating a probable score from the answer key, it helps to know exactly how marks are awarded and deducted in the OSSSC CRE Prelims exam.

  • Each correct answer carries 1 mark.
  • Each incorrect answer attracts a negative marking of 0.25 mark.
  • No marks are deducted for questions left unattempted.

Formula to calculate score:

Score = (Number of Correct Answers × 1) − (Number of Incorrect Answers × 0.25)

Steps to Calculate Your Probable Score

  1. Download the OSSSC RI ARI Answer Key 2026 PDF.
  2. Compare each of your marked responses with the official key.
  3. Count the total correct answers and multiply by 1.
  4. Count the total incorrect answers and multiply by 0.25.
  5. Subtract the negative marks from the total correct marks to get your probable score.

What is the UP Home Guard Final Answer Key 2026?

The final answer key is the official, verified set of correct answers for the UP Home Guard written examination, published by after carefully reviewing all candidate objections raised against the provisional key. Understanding the difference between a provisional and a final answer key is important for every aspirant.

After the provisional answer key was released on 7 May 2026, candidates were given a window from 7 May to 10 May 2026 (midnight) to submit evidence-based objections against any answers they believed were incorrect. The board's subject experts then evaluated all objections received. As per the official notification, objections related to two questions were found to be valid across all six examination shifts. The final answer key incorporates these corrections, and the UP Home Guard Result 2026 has been computed based on this verified final key. No further objections or challenges are entertained after the release of the final answer key.

Direct Link to Download UP Home Guard Final Answer Key 2026

Candidates can access the final answer key and result directly through the official portal. Use the login credentials you registered with to access your personal score card and final answer key.

  • Final Answer Key Direct Link: UP Home Guard Final Answer Key 2026
  • Official Website: uppbpb.gov.in

How to Download UP Home Guard Final Answer Key 2026 - Step-by-Step

Downloading the final answer key is a straightforward process. Follow these steps carefully to access your answer key and score card from the official portal without any confusion.

  1. Visit the Official Portal: Go to uppbpb.gov.in or the official website at uppbpb.gov.in.
  2. Click the Answer Key / Result Link: On the homepage, look for the notification titled "UP Home Guard Final Answer Key 2026" or "Home Guard Written Exam Result 2026."
  3. Enter Login Credentials: Input your Roll Number or Registration Number along with your Date of Birth (DD/MM/YYYY) and your Question Booklet Number where required.
  4. Click Submit: Press the Submit button to proceed to your personal result and answer key page.
  5. View Your Answer Key and Score: Your set-wise final answer key (Set A, B, C, or D) along with your score card will be displayed on the screen.
  6. Download and Save: Download the PDF and take a printout for future reference, especially for the upcoming Physical Standard Test (PST) and Document Verification stages.

 

Once you log in and download your scorecard, make sure to verify the following details carefully. Any discrepancy should be reported to immediately through official channels.

  • Candidate's Full Name
  • Father's Name
  • Date of Birth
  • Roll Number / Registration Number
  • Marks Obtained in Written Examination
  • Qualifying Status (Qualified / Not Qualified)
  • Category
  • District Allotted

UP Home Guard Cut-Off Marks 2026 - Category-Wise

The cut-off marks for the UP Home Guard Written Exam 2026 have been released district-wise and category-wise along with the result on 28 June 2026. Here are some important benchmarks every candidate should be aware of.

  • Minimum Qualifying Marks: Every candidate must secure at least 25% marks (25 out of 100) in the written examination to remain in contention. Candidates scoring below 25% are automatically disqualified from the recruitment process, regardless of category.
  • Safe Score (General/OBC): According to experts, a score of 72 marks or above is considered a safe score for General and OBC category candidates.
  • PET Preparation Range: Candidates who have correctly answered approximately 70 to 75 questions are advised to immediately begin preparation for the Physical Efficiency Test (PET/PST).
  • No Negative Marking: There is no negative marking in the UP Home Guard written examination. Every correct answer carries equal marks.

Note: Exact district-wise and category-wise cut-off marks are available on the official website. Candidates are advised to check the official portal for their specific district's cut-off figures.

Validity of the Final Answer Key - What Changed from Provisional to Final

The transition from a provisional to a final answer key is a standard and transparent process that ensures fairness to all candidates. Here is what happened between the provisional and final answer key stages for the UP Home Guard 2026 recruitment.

  • The provisional answer key was released on 7 May 2026.
  • Candidates were allowed to submit evidence-based objections from 7 May to 10 May 2026 (midnight).
  • Subject experts reviewed all submitted objections thoroughly.
  • Objections about two questions were found to be valid across all six examination shifts and were corrected in the final answer key.
  • The corrected final answer key formed the basis for result computation and merit list preparation.
  • No further challenges or objections are accepted after the release of the final answer key.

What Happens Next After the UP Home Guard Final Answer Key 2026?

Clearing the written examination is the first major step in the Home Guard selection process. Candidates who have qualified in the written test and appear on the merit list must prepare for the subsequent stages of the recruitment process.

Next Stages in UP Home Guard Recruitment 2026

  1. Document Verification (DV): Shortlisted candidates will be called for document verification. All original certificates, identity proofs, educational documents, and category certificates must be produced at this stage. Any mismatch or missing documents can lead to disqualification.
  2. Physical Standard Test (PST): Candidates must meet the prescribed physical standards regarding height, weight, and chest measurements as per norms.
  3. Physical Efficiency Test (PET): This test evaluates candidates on running, and other physical fitness parameters. Only those who pass the PST proceed to PET.
  4. Final Merit List: The final selection and merit list for all 41,424 Home Guard (Swayamsevak) posts will be prepared based on performance across all stages. The written examination marks form the primary basis for the final merit list.

About UPSC Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination 2026

The ISS Examination is one of the premier competitive exams conducted by UPSC to recruit officers for Group A and Group B posts in the Indian Statistical Service. Understanding the exam structure helps candidates correctly interpret the provisional answer key.

The Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination is conducted annually by the Union Public Service Commission to fill vacancies in the Indian Statistical Service, one of India's organised Group A Central Services. The exam tests candidates on subjects including Statistics, General English, and General Studies. The Statistics papers are the most technical and weightage-heavy components of the exam. The provisional answer key released covers the objective/multiple-choice components of the Statistics papers.

ISS Examination Paper Structure

How to Raise Objections Against UPSC ISS Provisional Answer Key 2026

If a candidate disagrees with any answer published in the provisional answer key, they can submit a formal representation to UPSC within the stipulated objection window period.

  • Download the provisional answer key PDF for the relevant paper.
  • Identify the question number(s) where you believe the answer is incorrect.
  • Prepare a written representation with supporting references from standard textbooks or study material.
  • Submit the representation to UPSC through the official channel specified in the answer key notification (typically by post or online submission to the UPSC office).
  • UPSC will review all representations received before publishing the Final Answer Key.

What Happens After the Provisional Answer Key?

After the provisional answer key is released and the objection window closes, UPSC reviews all valid representations before publishing the Final Answer Key.

Once the objection period ends, UPSC's subject matter experts review all representations submitted by candidates. Valid objections where an answer is found to be incorrect based on credible references result in changes to the final answer key. The Final Answer Key is then published on the official website. The final marks are computed based on the final (not provisional) answer key, which forms the basis for merit list preparation and eventual selection to the Indian Statistical Service.

Role Snapshot
Robotics Simulation Engineer

By artefacts In jobs

Artefacts is building a set of software tools for robotics software developers, facilitating Continuous Simulation in their workflow and tight integration with CI. We hope to help them take on the challenge of creating an advanced robotized world that will enable a more efficient and environmentally friendly society. We also believe that emerging AI techniques will dramatically change the way robotics software is built.

The Role

The role focuses on creating tools to help robotic engineers simulate and test their robots in rich and relevant virtual environments.

You will work closely with engineers working on robotics who will use the tools you are building.

This means

  • Create parametric / procedural 3d environments
  • Integrate AI tools to generate simulations or assets from text, images, etc.
  • Customization / tweaking of simulation engine performance for simulation at scale
  • Implement custom sensor models in simulation

If you are interested in the role

Please consider contacting us to apply! We expect a few things from you:

  • Enthusiasm and interest toward building realistic 3D environments as well as robotics and AI.
  • You will have room for growth, and many challenges.
  • We are enthusiastic and interested in our own specialties!
  • Ready to join a startup.
  • It can be messy, and requires personal commitment.
  • We expect you to work with us, not for us. We would like to see what you have done already.
  • Any publicly visible work such as open source contributions, personal blogs, Medium contributions, published paper etc.
  • Any publicly visible accounts such as Github, StackExchange etc.
  • Presentations at meetups / conferences?
  • Work / Projects you are particularly proud of

In terms of technologies and skills, we are interested in experience with:

  • Rust, Python or C++ or development experience
  • Experience using or building 3D Engines (Unreal, Unity, Ogre3D â¦) and physics simulation (Dart, ODE, PhysX)
  • Experience with parametric 3D modeling (Blender nodes, OpenSCADâ¦)
  • Experience with generative AI for 3D/CAD

Below are optional

  • Experience with robotics or robotics simulators
  • Experience with Photogrammetry / Nerf
  • Experience with cloud computing / high performance computing
  • Experience with GIS data sources
  • Experience with generative AI building or training ML models
  • Experience with 3D printing
  • Experience in UI/UX design

The ideal candidate

If You Score Yourself High On All The Items, We Definitely Hope For a Chance To Talk With You. We Will Consider Some Extras

  • Experience with âreal worldâ robot applications.
  • A real passion for Simulation Software or building Interactive Environments.
  • Graduate degree in related disciplines.
  • Degree is not necessary to apply, but if a work-visa is required, can make the visa-application process difficult without extensive, related work experience
  • The role would benefit from advanced analytical skills.

Application stages: Getting to know each other

We hope applying to work with us is a great experience. We value your time and your interest! We think the best way to decide working together is first to know more of each other, starting with us sharing our online profiles.

We propose meeting a number of times, primarily online, and freely talk about you, about us, and about what we could achieve together.

As much as we would like to meet every applicant, we expect first reading about your motivation for applying, and seeing your past achievements. This should give us a chance to reply early whether we should meet for the occasion. We promise to reply to each serious application.

In Short, Here Is a Typical Application Flow

  • You apply, sending us a resume and a cover letter. Again, we value very much seeing your public contributions.
  • We invite you for a first online meeting, or explain why we may not meet this time.
  • We may organize other meetings, for you and us to know better, sometimes on site.
  • We expect to make decisions relatively rapidly.
  • We may ask for references.

To apply, send an email at jobs at this domain.

Conditions and Team Membership

How We Work Together Is In Flux, As The Team And Company Grow. We Aim At Adapting Working Conditions As We All See Fit. Currently

  • We encourage asking âwhyâ.
  • Inclusive.
  • Personal growth-oriented environment.
  • Honest salaries.
  • No bonus culture.
  • Modern offices within 5 min walking distance from Shinjuku station (the building is a few years old).
  • Some prefer remote work, some office work, some change every day.
  • We gather at the office when needed.
  • We breathe open source, when it makes sense.
  • Medical checkup support in Tokyo.
  • We love challenges and opportunities that make us evolve.
  • Full or part time as you prefer. We usually start with a three-month contract to start working together.
  • Remote-first team. Preference for candidates in the JST timezone or so, and candidates in Japan (hardware!)

We hope these items paint a constructive image of our work style. All these items depend on the team, and your presence will influence them, as a partner.

Back to Blog

Youâll partner closely with Data to turn behavioral signals into segmentation and triggers, and with Product to keep lifecycle nudges tightly aligned with the in-app experience.

  • Raise the bar on experimentation: Youâll run a continuous A/B testing program (hypotheses, tests, learnings, iterations) to improve existing flows and challenge our current lifecycle map. Every decision should be grounded in evidence, not intuition.

  • Take CRM to the next level with AI: Youâll use AI to automate the operational grind (segmentation, copy iteration, QA, reporting) and unlock what we couldnât run manually: sharper personalization, faster experimentation cycles, and richer lifecycle logic.   • Drive growth across the company: Youâll work hand-in-hand with Product, Data, User Acquisition, and Brand so CRM compounds alongside everything else weâre building.

INNERGY is transforming the woodworking industry with purpose built, cloud based ERP software designed exclusively for custom manufacturers. Our platform helps businesses operate smarter, faster, and more efficiently while seamlessly connecting design, production, and delivery for teams creating architectural millwork, cabinetry, and casework.

What truly sets INNERGY apart is our people. Founded in 2016, we are a globally distributed team of 200 plus professionals united by deep software expertise and a shared passion for solving meaningful, real world problems. We value collaboration, creativity, and ownership, and we are intentional about building not only powerful products, but also a culture where people feel supported, heard, and inspired to do their best work.

With strong momentum and the recent acquisition of Microvellum, a trusted leader in design to manufacturing solutions for the woodworking industry, INNERGY is entering an exciting new phase of growth. This combination expands our capabilities, deepens our industry impact, and accelerates our vision of delivering a truly connected, end to end platform for custom manufacturers.

Job Description

We are seeking a strategic, execution-oriented Director of Customer Success to lead and unify the post-sale customer experience across INNERGY ERP and Microvellum CAD/CAM.

This leader will own the Customer Success operating system, including service model design, customer segmentation, tooling, performance management, and scalable enablement. The mandate is to build a consistent, measurable, and scalable CS organization that drives adoption, retention, expansion, and long-term customer value across all products and regions.

This role oversees a globally distributed organization of approximately Customer Success professionals, including team leads and Customer Success Managers. The Director brings a private equity mindset, balancing customer experience excellence with operational rigor, disciplined metrics, and scalable execution.

A core focus of this role is aligning the CS team around one unified post-sale strategy while leveraging AI, automation, and 1-to-many enablement to drive outcomes without linear headcount growth.

  • Drive measurable improvement in health model integrity and proactive outreach effectiveness through platforms such as HubSpot CSP and AI-enabled workflows.

  • Use data to inform capacity planning, prioritization, and segmentation strategy.
  • Implement strong performance management practices, including clear goals, accountability, and continuous coaching.

Scalable Customer Enablement

  • Design and execute service models that enable growth without proportional headcount increases.

  • Strengthen alignment with Sales, Product, Engineering, and RevOps to ensure clear handoffs and shared accountability for customer outcomes.
  • Coach leaders to elevate ownership, strategic thinking, and measurable impact.

Qualifications

  • Proven leadership experience in Customer Success and/or Customer Support within a SaaS, ERP, or complex software environment.
  • Experience operating in private equityâbacked organizations, including navigating rapid growth, change, and operational rigor.

  • Strong operational mindset with experience owning metrics, performance management, and service operations.
  • Track record of delivering scalable, world-class customer experiences without linear headcount growth.
  • Experience leveraging AI, automation, and 1-to-many enablement to improve efficiency and customer outcomes.
  • Exceptional leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
  • Experience supporting globally distributed teams and customers across multiple regions and time zones.
  • Familiarity with ERP, manufacturing, woodworking, cabinetry, or adjacent industries is a plus.

What Success Looks Like

  • Improved retention and Net Revenue Retention
